```{r}
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PLOT SAVE TOGGLES
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Set to TRUE to save plots for each section, FALSE to skip.

save_climatology   <- TRUE   # Section 5:  Spaghetti climatology (min/max temp, salinity, discharge)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ENVIRONMENTAL FACTOR TOGGLES
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Set to TRUE to include each environmental factor in downstream analyses
# (seasonal indices, lag correlations, predictor selection, predictive models).
# Set to FALSE to exclude. Data is still loaded but will not enter the
# predictor catalog. At minimum, one temperature metric must remain TRUE.

use_temp_min   <- FALSE    # Min water temperature (upwelling proxy)
use_temp_max   <- TRUE    # Max water temperature (thermal stress proxy)

use_cuti       <- FALSE    # CUTI  — coastal upwelling transport index

# ── Validation: at least one temperature metric must be active ────────────
stopifnot("At least one of use_temp_min or use_temp_max must be TRUE" =
            use_temp_min || use_temp_max)

cat("\n--- Active environmental factors ---\n")
env_toggles <- c(
  `Min temp`  = use_temp_min,  `Max temp`   = use_temp_max,
  BEUTI       = use_beuti,     CUTI         = use_cuti,
  Salinity    = use_salinity,  Discharge    = use_discharge,
  PDO         = use_pdo
)
cat(paste0("  ", names(env_toggles), ": ", ifelse(env_toggles, "ON", "OFF"),
           collapse = "\n"), "\n")
```

## Helper functions
```{r}
# ── Helper: Pearson r and p-value for a pair of vectors ─────────────────────
# Returns named vector c(r, p). Requires at least 5 complete pairs.
cor_p <- function(x, y) {
  d <- data.frame(x = x, y = y) %>% na.omit()
  if (nrow(d) > 4) {
    ct <- cor.test(d$x, d$y)
    c(r = unname(ct$estimate), p = unname(ct$p.value))
  } else {
    c(r = NA_real_, p = NA_real_)
  }
}

# ── Helper: tidy ACF/PACF computation ──────────────────────────────────────
# Returns a tibble with lag, acf value, and 95% CI bound.
tidy_acf <- function(x, lag_max = 10, type = "correlation") {
  x_clean <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x_clean) < 10) return(NULL)
  ac  <- acf(x_clean, lag.max = lag_max, type = type, plot = FALSE)
  ci  <- qnorm(0.975) / sqrt(length(x_clean))   # 95% Bartlett bound
  tibble(
    lag  = as.numeric(ac$lag),
    acf  = as.numeric(ac$acf),
    ci   = ci,
    type = type
  )
}

# ── Helper: tidy spectral analysis ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Returns tibble with freq, period, spectral density. Uses Daniell kernel smoothing.
tidy_spec <- function(x, series_name) {
  x_clean <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x_clean) < 12) return(NULL)
  x_interp <- approx(seq_along(x), x, xout = seq_along(x))$y
  sp <- spec.pgram(x_interp, spans = c(3, 3), taper = 0.1, plot = FALSE)
  tibble(
    freq    = sp$freq,
    period  = 1 / sp$freq,
    spec    = sp$spec,
    series  = series_name
  )
}

# ── Helper: Haversine distance (km) ────────────────────────────────────────
hav <- function(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) {
  R <- 6371
  p1 <- lat1 * pi / 180; p2 <- lat2 * pi / 180
  dp <- (lat2 - lat1) * pi / 180
  dl <- (lon2 - lon1) * pi / 180
  a  <- sin(dp/2)^2 + cos(p1) * cos(p2) * sin(dl/2)^2
  2 * R * asin(sqrt(a))
}
```

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SECTION 3: DATA LOADING
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Load data
```{r}

# ── Temperature data at three temporal resolutions ─────────────────────────
wtmp_daily        <- read_excel("02_data/Environmental Data/daily_wtmp_summary.xlsx", sheet = "data")
wtmp_half_month   <- read_excel("02_data/Environmental Data/half_monthly_wtmp_summary.xlsx", sheet = "data")
wtmp_monthly      <- read_excel("02_data/Environmental Data/monthly_wtmp_summary.xlsx", sheet = "data")

# ── Ensure month and year are numeric where they exist ─────────────────────
coerce_if_exists <- function(df) {
  if ("month" %in% names(df)) df <- df %>% mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month))
  if ("year"  %in% names(df)) df <- df %>% mutate(year  = as.numeric(.data$year))
  df
}

wtmp_daily      <- coerce_if_exists(wtmp_daily)
wtmp_half_month <- coerce_if_exists(wtmp_half_month)
wtmp_monthly    <- coerce_if_exists(wtmp_monthly)

# ── Station metadata (names, coordinates) ──────────────────────────────────
stations          <- read_excel("02_data/Environmental Data/Station Names.xlsx", sheet = "data")
wtmp_daily        <- left_join(wtmp_daily, stations, by = 'station')
wtmp_half_month   <- left_join(wtmp_half_month, stations, by = 'station')
wtmp_monthly      <- left_join(wtmp_monthly, stations, by = 'station')

# ── Razor clam recruitment data ────────────────────────────────────────────
dat          <- read_excel("02_data/razor-clam-season-summary-1997-2025.xlsx", sheet = "data")

# ── Shell length / age structure data ─────────────────────────────────────
# Individual clam measurements from summer stock assessments (1997–2025).
# Each row = one clam with shell length (mm), estimated age, size class,
# and age class assignments.
#
# GROWTH MODEL: von Bertalanffy parameters from Cheng & Kuk (2002) model
# fitted to WA capture-recapture data (2005–2007):
#   Copalis:    L∞ = 143.17 mm (SE 1.78), K = 1.00/yr (SE 0.06)
#   Long Beach: L∞ = 141.67 mm (SE 1.00), K = 0.98/yr (SE 0.04)
# Source: Cheng et al., "Modelling the growth of razor clam (Siliqua patula)
#         in Washington State coast" — WDFW/UW mark-recapture study.
# Northern beaches (Kalaloch, Mocrocks) use Copalis parameters (closest
# study site); Twin Harbors uses Long Beach parameters (closest study site).
#
# von Bertalanffy: L(t) = L∞ × (1 - exp(-K × t))
# Inverse:         t = -ln(1 - L/L∞) / K
#
# Size-at-age implications (Copalis / Long Beach):
#   Age 0.5: 56 / 55 mm    Age 1.0: 91 / 89 mm
#   Age 1.5: 111 / 109 mm  Age 2.0: 124 / 122 mm
#   Age 3.0: 136 / 134 mm  Age 5.0: 142 / 141 mm

sl_raw <- read_excel("02_data/shell_length_data-summary/All_Beaches_shell_lengths_1997-2025.xlsx",
                      sheet = "All_Clams_Raw")

# ── Beach-level yearly summaries (pre-computed) ────────────────────────────
sl_summary_all <- read_excel("02_data/shell_length_data-summary/All_Beaches_shell_lengths_1997-2025.xlsx",
                              sheet = "Year_Summary_All_Beaches")

cat("\n--- Shell length data loaded ---\n")
cat("Total individual measurements:", nrow(sl_raw), "\n")
cat("Beaches:", paste(unique(sl_raw$beach), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Year range:", min(sl_raw$survey_year), "–", max(sl_raw$survey_year), "\n")

# ── WA-specific von Bertalanffy growth parameters ─────────────────────────
# Beach-specific parameters from Cheng et al. mark-recapture study.
# Copalis parameters applied to northern beaches not in the study.
vb_params <- tibble(
  beach  = c("Kalaloch", "Mocrocks", "Copalis", "Twin Harbors", "Long Beach"),
  Linf   = c(143.17,     143.17,     143.17,    141.67,         141.67),
  K      = c(1.00,       1.00,       1.00,      0.98,           0.98),
  source = c("Copalis (proxy)", "Copalis (proxy)", "Copalis (study)",
             "Long Beach (study)", "Long Beach (study)")
)

cat("\n--- von Bertalanffy growth parameters (WA study) ---\n")
print(vb_params)

# ── Recalculate est_age_yr using WA-specific beach parameters ─────────────
# Replaces any previous age estimate (e.g., from California equation) with
# the WA mark-recapture growth model.
sl_raw <- sl_raw %>%
  left_join(vb_params %>% select(beach, Linf, K), by = "beach") %>%
  mutate(
    # von Bertalanffy inverse: t = -ln(1 - L/Linf) / K
    # Clamp length to < Linf to avoid log(0) or negative values
    length_clamped = pmin(length_mm, Linf - 0.1),
    est_age_yr = -log(1 - length_clamped / Linf) / K
  ) %>%
  select(-length_clamped)

cat("\n--- Age estimates recalculated using WA growth parameters ---\n")
cat("Age range:", round(range(sl_raw$est_age_yr, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "years\n")
sl_raw %>%
  group_by(beach) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_age = round(mean(est_age_yr, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max_age  = round(max(est_age_yr, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    Linf     = first(Linf),
    K        = first(K),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print()

# ── Reassign size classes and age classes based on WA growth model ─────────
# Size classes remain the same (defined by WDFW management thresholds):
#   Pre-recruit: ≤75 mm   Small recruit: 76–100 mm
#   Medium recruit: 101–120 mm   Large recruit: >120 mm
#
# Age class labels updated to reflect WA growth rates:
#   At 75mm:  ~0.74 yr (Copalis) / ~0.77 yr (Long Beach)
#   At 100mm: ~1.20 yr (Copalis) / ~1.25 yr (Long Beach)
#   At 120mm: ~1.82 yr (Copalis) / ~1.92 yr (Long Beach)
sl_raw <- sl_raw %>%
  mutate(
    size_class = case_when(
      length_mm <= 75  ~ "Pre-recruit (<=75 mm)",
      length_mm <= 100 ~ "Small recruit (76-100 mm)",
      length_mm <= 120 ~ "Medium recruit (101-120 mm)",
      TRUE             ~ "Large recruit (>120 mm)"
    ),
    age_class = case_when(
      length_mm <= 75  ~ "Young-of-year (<0.8 yr)",
      length_mm <= 100 ~ "Juvenile (0.8-1.2 yr)",
      length_mm <= 120 ~ "Sub-adult (1.2-1.9 yr)",
      TRUE             ~ "Adult (1.9+ yr)"
    )
  )

cat("Size classes:", paste(unique(sl_raw$size_class), collapse = " | "), "\n")
cat("Age classes:", paste(unique(sl_raw$age_class), collapse = " | "), "\n")

# ── Define age class → lag mapping (biological interpretation) ────────────
# Updated with WA growth parameters. Age boundaries are approximate
# midpoints across the two beach-specific parameter sets.
age_class_config <- tibble(
  age_class     = c("Young-of-year (<0.8 yr)", "Juvenile (0.8-1.2 yr)",
                     "Sub-adult (1.2-1.9 yr)", "Adult (1.9+ yr)"),
  size_class    = c("Pre-recruit (<=75 mm)", "Small recruit (76-100 mm)",
                     "Medium recruit (101-120 mm)", "Large recruit (>120 mm)"),
  short_label   = c("YOY", "Juvenile", "Sub-adult", "Adult"),
  age_min_yr    = c(0.0, 0.75, 1.2, 1.9),
  age_max_yr    = c(0.75, 1.2, 1.9, 7.0),
  # Lags focused on RECRUITMENT signal (when were these clams spawned?)
  # based on WA von Bertalanffy growth model (Cheng et al.):
  #   YOY (≤75mm, <0.75 yr):       spawned in survey year → lag 0
  #   Juvenile (76–100mm, ~1 yr):   spawned this/last year → lag 0–1
  #   Sub-adult (101–120mm, ~1.5 yr): spawned 1–2 years ago → lag 1–2
  #   Adult (>120mm, 1.9+ yr):      spawned 2–5+ years ago → lag 2–5
  # Adults exclude lag 0–1 to isolate the recruitment signal from survival.
  spawn_lag_min = c(0, 0, 1, 2),
  spawn_lag_max = c(0, 1, 2, 5),
  # Color for plotting
  color         = c("#2166AC", "#66BD63", "#F46D43", "#9E0142")
)

cat("\n--- Age class → lag configuration (WA growth model) ---\n")
print(age_class_config %>% select(short_label, age_min_yr, age_max_yr, spawn_lag_min, spawn_lag_max))

# ── Compute age-class-specific SAMPLE counts per beach × year ─────────────
# These are raw counts from transect measurements — used for descriptive plots
# (histograms, proportions, violins) but NOT for abundance modeling.
sl_age_counts <- sl_raw %>%
  group_by(survey_year, beach, size_class, age_class) %>%
  summarise(n_clams = n(),
            mean_length_mm = mean(length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_length_mm = median(length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_age = mean(est_age_yr, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_length = sd(length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(age_class_config %>% select(age_class, short_label, color,
                                         spawn_lag_min, spawn_lag_max),
            by = "age_class")

# ── Compute total clams per beach × year for proportions ──────────────────
sl_totals <- sl_raw %>%
  group_by(survey_year, beach) %>%
  summarise(n_total = n(), .groups = "drop")

sl_age_counts <- sl_age_counts %>%
  left_join(sl_totals, by = c("survey_year", "beach")) %>%
  mutate(proportion = n_clams / n_total,
         pct = round(proportion * 100, 1))

cat("\n--- Age-class sample counts: dimensions ---\n")
cat("Rows:", nrow(sl_age_counts), "\n")
cat("Beach × year × age class combinations\n")

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PROPORTION-WEIGHTED ABUNDANCE ESTIMATION
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The estimation workbooks (e.g., TH_2024.xls) show that:
#   1. Every clam counted in transect plots is also measured for shell length
#   2. Raw counts are expanded to beach-wide abundance via density × area
#   3. Expansion is done separately for ALL clams, pre-recruits (≤75mm), 
#      and recruits (>75mm)
#   4. The `dat` table stores the GRAND MEAN abundance estimates
#
# The shell length measurements come FROM these same transect counts, so:
#   - Sample proportions of each size class = population proportions
#   - All pre-recruits (≤75mm) are YOY by definition
#   - Within recruits: proportions of Small/Medium/Large map to Juvenile/Sub-adult/Adult
#
# To get age-class-specific ESTIMATED ABUNDANCE:
#   YOY_est      = pre_recruits (from dat)
#   Juvenile_est = recruits × (n_small_rec / n_total_rec_measured)
#   SubAdult_est = recruits × (n_med_rec   / n_total_rec_measured)
#   Adult_est    = recruits × (n_lg_rec    / n_total_rec_measured)
#
# This properly scales sample proportions to beach-wide population estimates.
# Using raw sample counts would be WRONG because they don't account for
# transect-to-beach area expansion or variable sampling effort between years.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── Step 1: Compute within-recruit proportions from shell length data ─────
recruit_props <- sl_raw %>%
  filter(size_class != "Pre-recruit (<=75 mm)") %>%
  group_by(survey_year, beach, size_class) %>%
  summarise(n_in_class = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(survey_year, beach) %>%
  mutate(n_total_rec_measured = sum(n_in_class),
         prop_within_rec = n_in_class / n_total_rec_measured) %>%
  ungroup()

# ── Step 2: Map size classes to age-class labels ──────────────────────────
recruit_props <- recruit_props %>%
  mutate(short_label = case_when(
    size_class == "Small recruit (76-100 mm)"   ~ "Juvenile",
    size_class == "Medium recruit (101-120 mm)" ~ "Sub-adult",
    size_class == "Large recruit (>120 mm)"     ~ "Adult",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

# ── Step 3: Join to dat to get estimated abundance ────────────────────────
# NOTE: dat may not be fully processed yet (sy column added later), so we
# extract survey_year directly from the season string.
dat_for_join <- dat %>%
  mutate(survey_year = as.integer(str_extract(season, "^[0-9]{4}"))) %>%
  select(survey_year, beach, pre_recruits, recruits)

# YOY = all pre-recruits
yoy_abundance <- dat_for_join %>%
  mutate(short_label = "YOY",
         est_abundance = pre_recruits,
         prop_within_rec = NA_real_) %>%
  select(survey_year, beach, short_label, est_abundance, prop_within_rec)

# Juvenile, Sub-adult, Adult = recruit abundance × proportion within recruits
recruit_abundance <- recruit_props %>%
  left_join(dat_for_join, by = c("survey_year", "beach")) %>%
  mutate(est_abundance = recruits * prop_within_rec) %>%
  select(survey_year, beach, short_label, est_abundance, prop_within_rec)

# Combine all four age classes
sl_estimated_abundance <- bind_rows(yoy_abundance, recruit_abundance) %>%
  filter(!is.na(est_abundance)) %>%
  left_join(age_class_config %>% select(short_label, spawn_lag_min, spawn_lag_max, color),
            by = "short_label") %>%
  mutate(log_est = log1p(est_abundance))

# ── Merge descriptive stats from sample counts ───────────────────────────
sl_estimated_abundance <- sl_estimated_abundance %>%
  left_join(
    sl_age_counts %>%
      select(survey_year, beach, short_label, n_clams, n_total, pct,
             mean_length_mm, median_length_mm, mean_age),
    by = c("survey_year", "beach", "short_label")
  )

cat("\n--- Proportion-weighted abundance estimation ---\n")
cat("Rows:", nrow(sl_estimated_abundance), "\n")
cat("Verification for Twin Harbors 2024:\n")
sl_estimated_abundance %>%
  filter(beach == "Twin Harbors", survey_year == 2024) %>%
  select(short_label, est_abundance, prop_within_rec, n_clams) %>%
  mutate(est_abundance = round(est_abundance)) %>%
  print()

cat("\nNote: est_abundance is the beach-wide population estimate (density × area).\n")
cat("      n_clams is the raw transect sample count (for reference only).\n")

# ── Also compute finer-grained size bins (10mm intervals) for histograms ──
sl_raw <- sl_raw %>%
  mutate(size_bin_10mm = cut(length_mm,
                              breaks = seq(0, 200, by = 10),
                              right = FALSE,
                              labels = paste0(seq(0, 190, by = 10), "-",
                                             seq(9, 199, by = 10), " mm")),
         size_bin_5mm = cut(length_mm,
                             breaks = seq(0, 200, by = 5),
                             right = FALSE))

cat("Shell length data preparation complete.\n")

# ── Upwelling indices (BEUTI and CUTI, daily, multi-latitude) ─────────────
# Source: Jacox et al. (2018), https://mjacox.com/upwelling-indices/
# Files contain daily values at 1° latitude bins (31–47°N).
# Each beach is assigned to its nearest latitude bin:
#   Long Beach (46.36°N)  → 46°N
#   Twin Harbors–Kalaloch → 47°N (northernmost available bin)

beuti_wide <- read.csv("02_data/Environmental Data/BEUTI_daily.csv", check.names = FALSE)
cuti_wide  <- read.csv("02_data/Environmental Data/CUTI_daily.csv",  check.names = FALSE)

# ── Beach → latitude bin mapping ─────────────────────────────────────────
beach_lat_bin <- tibble(
  beach   = c("Long Beach", "Twin Harbors", "Copalis", "Mocrocks", "Kalaloch"),
  lat_bin = c("46N",        "47N",          "47N",     "47N",      "47N")
)

# ── Pivot BEUTI to long format (date × latitude) ────────────────────────
beuti_long <- beuti_wide %>%
  mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month), year = as.numeric(.data$year), day = as.numeric(.data$day)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = matches("^\\d+N$"), names_to = "lat_bin", values_to = "beuti") %>%
  filter(lat_bin %in% c("46N", "47N"))

cuti_long <- cuti_wide %>%
  mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month), year = as.numeric(.data$year), day = as.numeric(.data$day)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = matches("^\\d+N$"), names_to = "lat_bin", values_to = "cuti") %>%
  filter(lat_bin %in% c("46N", "47N"))

# ── Combine BEUTI + CUTI daily, join to beach mapping ────────────────────
upwell_daily <- beuti_long %>%
  left_join(cuti_long, by = c("year", "month", "day", "lat_bin")) %>%
  left_join(beach_lat_bin, by = "lat_bin", relationship = "many-to-many")

# ── Aggregate to monthly means per beach ─────────────────────────────────
upwell_monthly <- upwell_daily %>%
  mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month)) %>%
  group_by(beach, year, month) %>%
  summarise(beuti = mean(beuti, na.rm = TRUE),
            cuti  = mean(cuti,  na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

cat("\n--- Upwelling indices loaded (interannual time series) ---\n")
cat("BEUTI file:", nrow(beuti_wide), "days,", min(beuti_wide$year), "–", max(beuti_wide$year), "\n")
cat("CUTI  file:", nrow(cuti_wide),  "days,", min(cuti_wide$year),  "–", max(cuti_wide$year),  "\n")
cat("Monthly upwelling rows (beach-specific):", nrow(upwell_monthly), "\n")

# Verify interannual variation (critical diagnostic)
cat("\n--- Interannual BEUTI variation check ---\n")
upwell_monthly %>%
  filter(.data$month %in% 5:6) %>%
  group_by(beach, year) %>%
  summarise(spawn_beuti = mean(beuti), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(beach) %>%
  summarise(sd = round(sd(spawn_beuti), 3),
            range = paste(round(range(spawn_beuti), 2), collapse = " to "),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  print()

# ── Salinity data (daily, station-level) ─────────────────────────────────
# Three Westport shelf buoys with lat/lon; will be IDW-blended to beaches
# like temperature in Section 4d.
salt_daily <- read_excel("02_data/Environmental Data/DailySalt.xlsx", sheet = "data") %>%
  mutate(
    date  = as.Date(Date),
    year  = year(date),
    month = as.numeric(month(date))
  ) %>%
  select(station, latitude, longitude, date, year, month,
         sal_mean = AvgSal, sal_min = minSal, sal_max = maxSal)

cat("\n--- Salinity data loaded ---\n")
cat("Stations:", paste(unique(salt_daily$station), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Date range:", as.character(range(salt_daily$date)), "\n")
cat("Rows:", nrow(salt_daily), "\n")

# ── Columbia River discharge (USGS gauge 14105700, The Dalles) ───────────
# Daily mean discharge in cubic feet per second (cfs), converted to m³/s.
# The Dalles is the last major gauge before the estuary and captures
# total basin runoff. Record extends from 1878; we use 1990–present.
# Higher discharge → stronger plume → lower nearshore salinity at Long Beach.

if (!use_discharge) {
  cat("\n--- Columbia River discharge: SKIPPED (use_discharge = FALSE) ---\n")
  cr_discharge <- NULL
} else {

cat("\n--- Downloading Columbia River discharge from USGS ---\n")

# Check for cached file first (fastest path)
discharge_cache <- "02_data/Environmental Data/columbia_discharge.csv"

cr_discharge <- if (file.exists(discharge_cache)) {
  cat("  Loading from cached file:", discharge_cache, "\n")
  read.csv(discharge_cache) %>% 
    mutate(date = as.Date(date), month = as.numeric(.data$month), year = as.numeric(.data$year))
} else {
  # Try multiple download methods to handle SSL/firewall issues
  result <- NULL
  
  # Method 1: read_waterdata_daily (requires httr2 >= 1.0.0)
  if (is.null(result)) {
    result <- tryCatch({
      cat("  Method 1: read_waterdata_daily()...\n")
      raw <- read_waterdata_daily(
        monitoring_location_id = "USGS-14105700",
        parameter_code = "00060", statistic_id = "00003",
        time = c("1990-01-01", as.character(Sys.Date()))
      )
      raw %>%
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
        filter(parameter_code == "00060") %>%
        rename(discharge_cfs = value) %>%
        mutate(date = as.Date(time), year = as.numeric(year(date)), month = as.numeric(month(date)),
               discharge_cms = discharge_cfs * 0.0283168) %>%
        filter(!is.na(discharge_cfs)) %>%
        select(date, year, month, discharge_cfs, discharge_cms)
    }, error = function(e) { cat("    Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }
  
  # Method 2: Direct download.file + jsonlite (often bypasses SSL issues)
  if (is.null(result)) {
    result <- tryCatch({
      cat("  Method 2: download.file + jsonlite...\n")
      api_url <- paste0(
        "https://api.waterdata.usgs.gov/ogcapi/v0/collections/daily/items",
        "?f=json&monitoring_location_id=USGS-14105700",
        "&parameter_code=00060&statistic_id=00003",
        "&time=1990-01-01/", format(Sys.Date(), "%Y-%m-%d"),
        "&limit=50000")
      tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
      download.file(api_url, tmp, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE, method = "auto")
      raw_json <- jsonlite::fromJSON(tmp)
      unlink(tmp)
      props <- raw_json$features$properties
      props %>% as_tibble() %>%
        mutate(date = as.Date(time), year = as.numeric(year(date)), month = as.numeric(month(date)),
               discharge_cfs = as.numeric(value),
               discharge_cms = discharge_cfs * 0.0283168) %>%
        filter(!is.na(discharge_cfs)) %>%
        select(date, year, month, discharge_cfs, discharge_cms)
    }, error = function(e) { cat("    Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }
  
  # Method 3: USGS tab-separated RDB format (different endpoint, simpler SSL)
  if (is.null(result)) {
    result <- tryCatch({
      cat("  Method 3: USGS waterdata RDB format...\n")
      rdb_url <- paste0(
        "https://waterdata.usgs.gov/nwis/dv?cb_00060=on&format=rdb",
        "&site_no=14105700&referred_module=sw",
        "&period=&begin_date=1990-01-01&end_date=", format(Sys.Date(), "%Y-%m-%d"))
      tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
      download.file(rdb_url, tmp, mode = "w", quiet = TRUE, method = "auto")
      lines <- readLines(tmp)
      unlink(tmp)
      # RDB files have comment lines starting with # and a header row
      data_start <- max(which(grepl("^#", lines))) + 1
      # Skip the format line (2nd header line)
      raw <- read.delim(text = paste(lines[c(data_start, (data_start+2):length(lines))],
                                      collapse = "\n"),
                         sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      # Column name varies; find the discharge column
      q_col <- grep("00060.*00003", names(raw), value = TRUE)[1]
      if (is.na(q_col)) stop("Discharge column not found in RDB output")
      raw %>%
        rename(discharge_cfs = !!q_col) %>%
        mutate(date = as.Date(datetime), year = as.numeric(year(date)), month = as.numeric(month(date)),
               discharge_cfs = as.numeric(discharge_cfs),
               discharge_cms = discharge_cfs * 0.0283168) %>%
        filter(!is.na(discharge_cfs)) %>%
        select(date, year, month, discharge_cfs, discharge_cms)
    }, error = function(e) { cat("    Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }
  
  if (is.null(result)) {
    cat("\n  ALL download methods failed (likely SSL/firewall issue).\n")
    cat("  MANUAL FIX: Download discharge data via browser and save as:\n")
    cat("    ", discharge_cache, "\n")
    cat("  Browser URL (paste into browser, then File > Save As .csv):\n")
    cat("    https://waterdata.usgs.gov/nwis/dv?cb_00060=on&format=rdb&site_no=14105700&begin_date=1990-01-01\n")
    cat("  Or run in a fresh R session: install.packages('httr2') then re-run this script.\n")
  }
  result
}

if (!is.null(cr_discharge)) {
  cat("Columbia River discharge loaded:", nrow(cr_discharge), "daily records\n")
  cat("Date range:", as.character(range(cr_discharge$date)), "\n")
  cat("Discharge range:", round(range(cr_discharge$discharge_cms, na.rm = TRUE)),
      "m³/s\n")
  # Cache for offline use
  if (!file.exists(discharge_cache)) {
    write.csv(cr_discharge, discharge_cache, row.names = FALSE)
    cat("  Cached to:", discharge_cache, "\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Columbia River discharge: NOT AVAILABLE\n")
}
}  # end if (use_discharge)

# ── Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) index (NCEI / ERSST v5) ────────────
# The PDO is the leading EOF of monthly North Pacific SST anomalies (>20°N).
# It is a basin-scale index — one value per month for the entire North Pacific.
# Positive PDO = warm SSTs along the Pacific Coast, cool interior North Pacific.
# Source: NCEI ERSST v5 PDO index (Mantua et al. 1997; Zhang et al. 1997).
# URL: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/cmb/ersst/v5/index/ersst.v5.pdo.dat
#
# Relevance to razor clams:
#   - PDO phase shifts are associated with multi-decadal changes in NE Pacific
#     marine ecosystem productivity (originally discovered via salmon production)
#   - Warm PDO → warmer coastal SSTs, altered upwelling, different plankton community
#   - Cool PDO → cooler coastal SSTs, potentially enhanced diatom production
#   - The PDO is coastwide — same value for all 5 beaches in every month.

if (!use_pdo) {
  cat("\n--- PDO: SKIPPED (use_pdo = FALSE) ---\n")
  pdo_monthly <- NULL
} else {

cat("\n--- Loading PDO index from NCEI ---\n")

pdo_cache <- "02_data/Environmental Data/pdo_index.csv"

pdo_monthly <- if (file.exists(pdo_cache)) {
  cat("  Loading from cached file:", pdo_cache, "\n")
  read.csv(pdo_cache, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month), year = as.numeric(.data$year))
} else {
  result <- NULL
  
  # Method 1: rsoi package (cleanest, handles parsing automatically)
  if (is.null(result)) {
    result <- tryCatch({
      cat("  Method 1: rsoi::download_pdo()...\n")
      if (!requireNamespace("rsoi", quietly = TRUE)) {
        install.packages("rsoi", quiet = TRUE)
      }
      raw <- rsoi::download_pdo()
      raw %>%
        select(year = Year, month = Month, pdo = PDO) %>%
        mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month), year = as.numeric(.data$year)) %>%
        filter(!is.na(pdo))
    }, error = function(e) { cat("    Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }
  
  # Method 2: Direct download from NCEI
  if (is.null(result)) {
    result <- tryCatch({
      cat("  Method 2: Direct download from NCEI...\n")
      pdo_url <- "https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/cmb/ersst/v5/index/ersst.v5.pdo.dat"
      tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".dat")
      download.file(pdo_url, tmp, mode = "w", quiet = TRUE, method = "auto")
      # Fixed-width format: Year followed by 12 monthly values
      lines <- readLines(tmp)
      unlink(tmp)
      # Skip header lines (lines starting with non-numeric characters)
      data_lines <- lines[grepl("^\\s*\\d{4}", lines)]
      pdo_raw <- read.table(text = data_lines, header = FALSE,
                             col.names = c("year", month.abb))
      pdo_raw %>%
        pivot_longer(cols = -year, names_to = "month_name", values_to = "pdo") %>%
        mutate(
          month = match(month_name, month.abb),
          pdo = ifelse(pdo > 90 | pdo < -90, NA_real_, pdo)  # sentinel values
        ) %>%
        filter(!is.na(pdo), !is.na(.data$month)) %>%
        select(year, month, pdo)
    }, error = function(e) { cat("    Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }
  
  # Method 3: JISAO/UW PDO page
  if (is.null(result)) {
    result <- tryCatch({
      cat("  Method 3: JISAO PDO data...\n")
      jisao_url <- "http://research.jisao.washington.edu/pdo/PDO.latest.txt"
      lines <- readLines(jisao_url)
      data_lines <- lines[grepl("^\\s*\\d{4}", lines)]
      pdo_raw <- read.table(text = data_lines, header = FALSE,
                             col.names = c("year", month.abb))
      pdo_raw %>%
        pivot_longer(cols = -year, names_to = "month_name", values_to = "pdo") %>%
        mutate(
          month = match(month_name, month.abb),
          pdo = ifelse(pdo > 90 | pdo < -90, NA_real_, pdo)
        ) %>%
        filter(!is.na(pdo), !is.na(.data$month)) %>%
        select(year, month, pdo)
    }, error = function(e) { cat("    Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }
  
  if (is.null(result)) {
    cat("\n  ALL PDO download methods failed.\n")
    cat("  MANUAL FIX: Download PDO data via browser and save as:\n")
    cat("    ", pdo_cache, "\n")
    cat("  URL: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/cmb/ersst/v5/index/ersst.v5.pdo.dat\n")
  }
  result
}

if (!is.null(pdo_monthly)) {
  cat("PDO index loaded:", nrow(pdo_monthly), "monthly records\n")
  cat("Year range:", min(pdo_monthly$year), "–", max(pdo_monthly$year), "\n")
  cat("PDO range:", round(range(pdo_monthly$pdo, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n")
  # Cache for offline use
  if (!file.exists(pdo_cache)) {
    write.csv(pdo_monthly, pdo_cache, row.names = FALSE)
    cat("  Cached to:", pdo_cache, "\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("PDO: NOT AVAILABLE\n")
}
}  # end if (use_pdo)

# ── SATURN-02 salinity (CMOP/CRITFC, NDBC 46096) ────────────────────────
# Location: 46.173°N, 124.127°W — Columbia River entrance / plume station.
# ~21 km from Long Beach. Measures plume-influenced salinity, which is the
# mechanistically relevant variable for Long Beach (Columbia plume dynamics).
# Data from CMOP ERDDAP server (data.stccmop.org); CT sensor at 35 m depth.
# Dataset: saturn02_3500_P_CT (conductivity-temperature instrument).

cat("\n--- Downloading SATURN-02 salinity from CMOP ERDDAP ---\n")

saturn02_cache <- "02_data/Environmental Data/saturn02_salinity.csv"

# Helper: process raw ERDDAP CSV into daily salinity format
process_saturn02_raw <- function(raw_csv_path) {
  raw <- read.csv(raw_csv_path, skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(raw) <- c("time", "salinity")
  raw %>%
    mutate(salinity = as.numeric(salinity)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(salinity), salinity > 0, salinity < 40) %>%
    mutate(datetime = as.POSIXct(time, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC"),
           date = as.Date(datetime), year = year(date), month = month(date),
           station = "SATURN-02", latitude = 46.17345, longitude = -124.12717) %>%
    group_by(station, latitude, longitude, date, year, month) %>%
    summarise(sal_mean = mean(salinity, na.rm = TRUE),
              sal_min = min(salinity, na.rm = TRUE),
              sal_max = max(salinity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
}

erddap_url <- paste0(
  "https://data.stccmop.org/erddap/tabledap/saturn02_3500_P_CT.csv",
  "?time,sea_water_practical_salinity",
  "&time>=2008-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "&sea_water_practical_salinity>0",
  "&sea_water_practical_salinity<40")

saturn02_sal <- if (file.exists(saturn02_cache)) {
  cat("  Loading from cached file:", saturn02_cache, "\n")
  cached <- read.csv(saturn02_cache, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if ("sal_mean" %in% names(cached)) {
    # Already in processed daily format
    cached %>% mutate(date = as.Date(date))
  } else if ("time" %in% names(cached) || "sea_water_practical_salinity" %in% names(cached)) {
    # Raw ERDDAP format — process and re-save
    cat("  Detected raw ERDDAP format — processing to daily...\n")
    processed <- process_saturn02_raw(saturn02_cache)
    write.csv(processed, saturn02_cache, row.names = FALSE)
    cat("  Re-saved in daily format.\n")
    processed
  } else {
    cat("  WARNING: Unrecognized format in cached file. Columns:", paste(names(cached), collapse = ", "), "\n")
    NULL
  }
} else {
  result <- NULL
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  
  # Method 1: system curl with -k (skip SSL verification)
  if (is.null(result)) {
    result <- tryCatch({
      cat("  Method 1: system curl -k (skip SSL verify)...\n")
      cmd <- sprintf('curl -k -s -o "%s" "%s"', tmp, erddap_url)
      exit_code <- system(cmd)
      if (exit_code != 0) stop("curl returned exit code ", exit_code)
      if (!file.exists(tmp) || file.size(tmp) < 100) stop("Downloaded file is empty or missing")
      process_saturn02_raw(tmp)
    }, error = function(e) { cat("    Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }
  
  # Method 2: download.file with curl method (uses R's curl binding)
  if (is.null(result)) {
    result <- tryCatch({
      cat("  Method 2: download.file (curl method)...\n")
      download.file(erddap_url, tmp, mode = "w", quiet = TRUE, method = "curl",
                    extra = "-k")  # -k = insecure, skips SSL verify
      if (!file.exists(tmp) || file.size(tmp) < 100) stop("Downloaded file is empty")
      process_saturn02_raw(tmp)
    }, error = function(e) { cat("    Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }
  
  # Method 3: download.file with wininet (Windows only — uses OS SSL stack)
  if (is.null(result) && .Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
    result <- tryCatch({
      cat("  Method 3: download.file (wininet method, Windows SSL)...\n")
      download.file(erddap_url, tmp, mode = "w", quiet = TRUE, method = "wininet")
      if (!file.exists(tmp) || file.size(tmp) < 100) stop("Downloaded file is empty")
      process_saturn02_raw(tmp)
    }, error = function(e) { cat("    Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }
  
  # Method 4: Direct read.csv (R's internal HTTP/SSL)
  if (is.null(result)) {
    result <- tryCatch({
      cat("  Method 4: read.csv (R internal SSL)...\n")
      process_saturn02_raw(erddap_url)
    }, error = function(e) { cat("    Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  }
  
  unlink(tmp)
  
  if (is.null(result)) {
    cat("\n  ALL download methods failed (SSL issue with data.stccmop.org).\n")
    cat("  MANUAL FIX — run this in a system terminal (not R), then re-run script:\n")
    cat('  curl -k "', erddap_url, '" -o saturn02_raw.csv\n', sep = "")
    cat("  Then in R:\n")
    cat('  raw <- read.csv("saturn02_raw.csv", skip = 1)\n')
    cat('  # ... or just copy saturn02_raw.csv to:\n')
    cat("    ", saturn02_cache, "\n")
    cat("  (The script will auto-detect and use it on next run.)\n")
  }
  result
}

if (!is.null(saturn02_sal)) {
  cat("SATURN-02 salinity loaded:", nrow(saturn02_sal), "daily records\n")
  cat("Date range:", as.character(range(saturn02_sal$date)), "\n")
  cat("Mean salinity range:", round(range(saturn02_sal$sal_mean, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "PSU\n")
  # Cache for offline use
  if (!file.exists(saturn02_cache)) {
    write.csv(saturn02_sal, saturn02_cache, row.names = FALSE)
    cat("  Cached to:", saturn02_cache, "\n")
  }
  
  # ── Bind SATURN-02 into salt_daily so IDW blending picks it up ──────────
  # Format to match salt_daily columns
  saturn02_for_bind <- saturn02_sal %>%
    select(station, latitude, longitude, date, year, month,
           sal_mean, sal_min, sal_max)
  
  salt_daily <- bind_rows(salt_daily, saturn02_for_bind)
  cat("SATURN-02 appended to salt_daily. Total rows:", nrow(salt_daily), "\n")
  cat("Stations now:", paste(unique(salt_daily$station), collapse = ", "), "\n")
} else {
  cat("SATURN-02: NOT AVAILABLE — Long Beach remains without local salinity\n")
}

# ── Ordering factors for beaches and seasons ───────────────────────────────
sort_season  <- read_excel("02_data/razor-clam-season-summary-1997-2025.xlsx", sheet = "sort_season") %>%
  mutate(season = factor(season, levels = unique(season), ordered = TRUE))

sort_beach   <- read_excel("02_data/razor-clam-season-summary-1997-2025.xlsx", sheet = "sort_beach") %>%
  mutate(Beach = factor(Beach, levels = unique(Beach), ordered = TRUE))

# ── 0. Drop the unneeded year column ─────────────────────────────────────────
dat <- dat %>% select(-year)

# ── Beach order vector (North to South) for consistent use throughout ──────
beach_order <- levels(sort_beach$Beach)
cat("Beach order (N to S):", paste(beach_order, collapse = " > "), "\n")
```

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SECTION 4: IDW TEMPERATURE BLENDING (ALL TIMESCALES)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

## IDW parameters and beach coordinates

```{r}
# Estimates water temperature at each razor clam beach by inverse-distance
# weighting (IDW) of nearby buoys within max_dist km. Computes blended mean,
# min, and max temperature simultaneously so downstream analyses can compare
# which metric has the strongest relationship with recruitment.

max_dist <- 50   # km radius — stations beyond this are excluded from blending
idwp     <- 3     # IDW power parameter: higher = closer stations dominate more

# ── 1. Beach coordinates ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
bc <- tibble(
  beach = c("Long Beach", "Twin Harbors", "Copalis", "Mocrocks", "Kalaloch"),
  blat  = c(46.361592,    46.855477,     47.133586,  47.238914,  47.606156),
  blon  = c(-124.069805, -124.118770,    -124.195585,-124.219583,-124.380790)
)
```

## 4a. Monthly IDW blending

```{r}
# ── Unique stations with valid coordinates from monthly data ───────────────
st <- wtmp_monthly %>%
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) %>%
  distinct(station, latitude, longitude)

# Distance lookup: every beach to every station with valid coordinates
bsd <- bc %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    ds = list(
      st %>% mutate(d = hav(blat, blon, latitude, longitude))
    )
  ) %>%
  unnest(ds) %>%
  select(beach, station, d) %>%
  ungroup()

# ── IDW blended monthly temperature: mean, min, max ────────────────────────
aym <- wtmp_monthly %>% 
  mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month)) %>% 
  distinct(year, month)   # all year-month combos in the data

wi <- bc %>%
  select(beach) %>%
  cross_join(aym) %>%
  left_join(bsd, by = "beach", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  left_join(
    wtmp_monthly %>% 
      mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month)) %>% 
      select(station, year, month, wtmp_mean, wtmp_min, wtmp_max, wtmp_sd),
    by = c("station", "year", "month"), relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(wtmp_mean), d <= max_dist) %>%
  mutate(w = 1 / d ^ idwp) %>%
  group_by(beach, year, month) %>%
  summarise(
    at       = weighted.mean(wtmp_mean, w = w),
    at_min   = weighted.mean(wtmp_min,  w = w),
    at_max   = weighted.mean(wtmp_max,  w = w),
    at_sd    = sqrt(weighted.mean(wtmp_sd^2, w = w)),
    ns       = n(),
    dom_stn  = station[which.max(w)],
    all_stns = paste(station, collapse = ", "),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

# ── Completeness diagnostic ────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat("\n--- Monthly IDW completeness ---\n")
wi %>%
  group_by(beach) %>%
  summarise(
    nf = n(),
    ne = n_distinct(wtmp_monthly$year) * 12,
    pc = round(nf / ne, 3),
    an = round(mean(ns), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print()

# ── Station attribution table (monthly) ───────────────────────────────────
# Which station names (from stations$Name) contribute to each beach?
stn_attr_monthly <- wi %>%
  select(beach, year, month, dom_stn, all_stns) %>%
  left_join(stations %>% select(station, Name), by = c("dom_stn" = "station")) %>%
  rename(dom_stn_name = Name)

cat("\n--- Dominant stations by beach (monthly) ---\n")
stn_attr_monthly %>%
  group_by(beach) %>%
  summarise(
    primary_station_id   = names(which.max(table(dom_stn))),
    primary_station_name = names(which.max(table(dom_stn_name))),
    all_contributing_ids = paste(unique(unlist(str_split(all_stns, ", "))), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print()

# ── Pivot to wide format for joining to clam data ─────────────────────────
ww <- wi %>%
  select(-dom_stn, -all_stns) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = month,
    values_from = c(at, at_min, at_max, at_sd, ns),
    names_glue  = "{.value}_m{month}"
  )

# Safety check: must be exactly one row per beach × year before joining to dat
stopifnot(nrow(ww) == nrow(distinct(ww, beach, year)))

# ── Join to dat ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
dat_wtmp <- dat %>%
  mutate(sy = as.integer(str_extract(season, "^[0-9]{4}"))) %>%
  left_join(ww, by = c("beach", "sy" = "year")) %>%
  select(-sy)

# ── NULL diagnostic: check coverage ───────────────────────────────────────
cat("\n--- Monthly temperature coverage in clam data ---\n")
dat_wtmp %>%
  select(beach, season, matches("^at_m[0-9]+$")) %>%
  pivot_longer(matches("^at_m[0-9]+$"), names_to = "mo", values_to = "tmp") %>%
  group_by(beach) %>%
  summarise(
    n  = n(),
    na = sum(is.na(tmp)),
    p  = round(na / n, 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print()
```

## 4b. Half-monthly IDW blending

```{r}
# ── IDW blended half-month temperature: mean, min, max ────────────────────────
# Half-month resolution (H1 = days 1–15, H2 = days 16–end) provides a finer
# temporal window for lag analysis — particularly useful for detecting whether
# the first or second half of key months (e.g. early vs late June spawning window)
# is more predictive of recruitment.

aymh <- wtmp_half_month %>% 
  mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month)) %>% 
  distinct(year, month, half)

st_hm <- wtmp_half_month %>%
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) %>%
  distinct(station, latitude, longitude)

bsd_hm <- bc %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    ds = list(st_hm %>% mutate(d = hav(blat, blon, latitude, longitude)))
  ) %>%
  unnest(ds) %>%
  select(beach, station, d) %>%
  ungroup()

wi_hm <- bc %>%
  select(beach) %>%
  cross_join(aymh) %>%
  left_join(bsd_hm, by = "beach", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  left_join(
    wtmp_half_month %>% 
      mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month)) %>% 
      select(station, year, month, half, wtmp_mean, wtmp_min, wtmp_max, wtmp_sd),
    by = c("station", "year", "month", "half"), relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(wtmp_mean), d <= max_dist) %>%
  mutate(w = 1 / d ^ idwp) %>%
  group_by(beach, year, month, half) %>%
  summarise(
    hm_mean = weighted.mean(wtmp_mean, w = w),
    hm_min  = weighted.mean(wtmp_min,  w = w),
    hm_max  = weighted.mean(wtmp_max,  w = w),
    hm_sd   = sqrt(weighted.mean(wtmp_sd^2, w = w)),
    ns      = n(),
    dom_stn = station[which.max(w)],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(period = paste0(.data$month, "_", .data$half))

# Half-month completeness check
cat("\n--- Half-monthly IDW completeness ---\n")
wi_hm %>%
  group_by(beach) %>%
  summarise(
    nf = n(),
    ne = n_distinct(wtmp_half_month$year) * 24,
    pc = round(nf / ne, 3),
    an = round(mean(ns), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print()

# Station attribution (half-monthly)
cat("\n--- Dominant stations by beach (half-monthly) ---\n")
wi_hm %>%
  group_by(beach) %>%
  summarise(
    primary_station_id = names(which.max(table(dom_stn))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(stations %>% select(station, Name), by = c("primary_station_id" = "station")) %>%
  rename(primary_station_name = Name) %>%
  print()
```

## 4c. Weekly IDW blending (from daily data)
```{r}
# ── Aggregate daily data to weekly summaries ──────────────────────────────
# Uses ISO week numbers via lubridate::isoweek(). Each week is identified by
# year + week number. Aggregation computes mean, min, max, and SD of daily
# temperatures within each station × year × week.
#
# IMPORTANT: lubridate masks base::date and also provides day(), month(), year()
# functions that can collide with column names in the daily data. We use
# lubridate extraction functions on the date_col to derive year/month/week
# rather than assuming those columns exist in the raw data.

# Diagnostic: print column names so we can confirm what's available
cat("\n--- wtmp_daily columns ---\n")
cat(paste(names(wtmp_daily), collapse = ", "), "\n")

# ── Step 1: Build a proper Date column + derive year/month/week ───────────
# The daily data may have a 'date' column, year/month/day columns, or both.
# We always derive wk_year, wk_month, week, and iso_year from the date using
# lubridate functions to avoid any column-name ambiguity.

if ("date" %in% names(wtmp_daily) && inherits(wtmp_daily$date, c("Date", "POSIXct", "POSIXlt"))) {
  # Date column already exists and is a proper date type — use it directly
  cat("Using existing 'date' column from wtmp_daily\n")
  wtmp_daily <- wtmp_daily %>%
    mutate(
      date_col = as.Date(.data$date),
      wk_year  = year(date_col),      # extract year from date
      wk_month = month(date_col),     # extract month from date
      week     = isoweek(date_col),
      iso_year = isoyear(date_col)
    )
} else if (all(c("year", "month", "day") %in% names(wtmp_daily))) {
  # Construct date from year/month/day columns
  # Use .data$ to avoid lubridate masking the 'day' column
  cat("Constructing date from year/month/day columns\n")
  wtmp_daily <- wtmp_daily %>%
    mutate(
      date_col = as.Date(paste(.data$year, .data$month, .data$day, sep = "-")),
      wk_year  = year(date_col),
      wk_month = month(date_col),
      week     = isoweek(date_col),
      iso_year = isoyear(date_col)
    )
} else {
  # Fallback: try to find any date-like column
  date_candidates <- names(wtmp_daily)[sapply(wtmp_daily, function(x) inherits(x, c("Date", "POSIXct")))]
  if (length(date_candidates) > 0) {
    cat("Using date candidate column:", date_candidates[1], "\n")
    wtmp_daily <- wtmp_daily %>%
      mutate(
        date_col = as.Date(.data[[date_candidates[1]]]),
        wk_year  = year(date_col),
        wk_month = month(date_col),
        week     = isoweek(date_col),
        iso_year = isoyear(date_col)
      )
  } else {
    stop("Cannot find or construct a date column in wtmp_daily. ",
         "Available columns: ", paste(names(wtmp_daily), collapse = ", "))
  }
}

# ── Step 2: Identify the temperature value column ─────────────────────────
# The daily data might call the temperature column 'wtmp', 'WTMP', 'temp', etc.
temp_col_candidates <- c("wtmp", "WTMP", "temp", "temperature", "wtmp_mean", "value")
temp_col <- intersect(temp_col_candidates, names(wtmp_daily))
if (length(temp_col) == 0) {
  cat("WARNING: No recognized temperature column found. Candidates tried:",
      paste(temp_col_candidates, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  cat("Available columns:", paste(names(wtmp_daily), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  temp_col <- NA_character_
} else {
  temp_col <- temp_col[1]
  cat("Using temperature column:", temp_col, "\n")
}

# ── Step 3: Weekly aggregation per station ────────────────────────────────
if (!is.na(temp_col)) {
  wtmp_weekly <- wtmp_daily %>%
    rename(temp_val = !!sym(temp_col)) %>%
    group_by(station, iso_year, week, latitude, longitude) %>%
    summarise(
      wtmp_mean = mean(temp_val, na.rm = TRUE),
      wtmp_min  = min(temp_val,  na.rm = TRUE),
      wtmp_max  = max(temp_val,  na.rm = TRUE),
      wtmp_sd   = sd(temp_val,   na.rm = TRUE),
      n_days    = sum(!is.na(temp_val)),
      # Dominant month: which month contributes the most days to this week
      month     = as.integer(names(which.max(table(wk_month)))),
      .groups   = "drop"
    ) %>%
    rename(year = iso_year) %>%
    # Replace Inf/-Inf from min/max on all-NA groups with NA
    mutate(
      across(c(wtmp_min, wtmp_max), ~ifelse(is.infinite(.), NA_real_, .)),
      wtmp_sd = ifelse(is.nan(wtmp_sd), NA_real_, wtmp_sd)
    ) %>%
    # Require at least 4 days for a valid weekly summary
    filter(n_days >= 4)
  
  cat("Weekly aggregation complete:", nrow(wtmp_weekly), "station-weeks\n")
} else {
  wtmp_weekly <- NULL
  cat("WARNING: Skipping weekly aggregation — no temperature column identified\n")
}

# ── Step 4: IDW blending for weekly resolution ────────────────────────────
# Only proceeds if weekly aggregation succeeded above.

wi_wk <- NULL   # initialize as NULL; downstream code checks for this

if (!is.null(wtmp_weekly) && nrow(wtmp_weekly) > 0) {
  
  st_wk <- wtmp_weekly %>%
    filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) %>%
    distinct(station, latitude, longitude)
  
  bsd_wk <- bc %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      ds = list(st_wk %>% mutate(d = hav(blat, blon, latitude, longitude)))
    ) %>%
    unnest(ds) %>%
    select(beach, station, d) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  aywk <- wtmp_weekly %>% 
    mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month)) %>% 
    distinct(year, week)
  
  wi_wk <- bc %>%
    select(beach) %>%
    cross_join(aywk) %>%
    left_join(bsd_wk, by = "beach", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    left_join(
      wtmp_weekly %>% 
        mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month)) %>% 
        select(station, year, week, month, wtmp_mean, wtmp_min, wtmp_max, wtmp_sd),
      by = c("station", "year", "week"), relationship = "many-to-many"
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(wtmp_mean), d <= max_dist) %>%
    mutate(w = 1 / d ^ idwp) %>%
    group_by(beach, year, week) %>%
    summarise(
      wk_mean = weighted.mean(wtmp_mean, w = w),
      wk_min  = weighted.mean(wtmp_min,  w = w),
      wk_max  = weighted.mean(wtmp_max,  w = w),
      wk_sd   = sqrt(weighted.mean(wtmp_sd^2, w = w)),
      month   = as.numeric(names(which.max(table(month)))),
      ns      = n(),
      dom_stn = station[which.max(w)],
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  # Weekly completeness check
  cat("\n--- Weekly IDW completeness ---\n")
  wi_wk %>%
    group_by(beach) %>%
    summarise(
      nf = n(),
      ne = n_distinct(wtmp_weekly$year) * 52,
      pc = round(nf / ne, 3),
      an = round(mean(ns), 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    print()
  
  # Station attribution (weekly)
  cat("\n--- Dominant stations by beach (weekly) ---\n")
  wi_wk %>%
    group_by(beach) %>%
    summarise(
      primary_station_id = names(which.max(table(dom_stn))),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    left_join(stations %>% select(station, Name), by = c("primary_station_id" = "station")) %>%
    rename(primary_station_name = Name) %>%
    print()
  
} else {
  cat("\n--- Weekly IDW: SKIPPED (daily aggregation failed or produced no data) ---\n")
  cat("The analysis will proceed with monthly and half-monthly timescales only.\n")
}
```

## 4d. Salinity IDW blending (monthly from daily)

```{r}
# ── IDW blended salinity at each beach ────────────────────────────────────
# Strategy: Only blend salinity from stations within 40 km of a beach.
# This ensures that salinity values represent genuinely local oceanographic
# conditions rather than extrapolating across water mass boundaries.
#
# With current station coverage (3 Westport shelf buoys + SATURN-02):
#   Copalis / Mocrocks  → Westport buoys within ~5–12 km  → good local data
#   Twin Harbors        → Westport buoys within ~33–36 km  → acceptable
#   Long Beach          → SATURN-02 within ~21 km (if available) → plume salinity
#   Kalaloch            → nearest station ~53 km → excluded (NA)
#
# FUTURE-PROOFING: If new buoy data is added to DailySalt.xlsx (or bound
# from ERDDAP as with SATURN-02), the code will automatically detect it,
# compute distances, and include it in the IDW blend for nearby beaches.
# No code changes are needed — just add rows to the input data.

sal_max_dist <- 40  # km — only use stations representing local conditions

# ── 1. Aggregate daily salinity to monthly per station ─────────────────────
salt_monthly <- salt_daily %>%
  mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month)) %>%
  group_by(station, latitude, longitude, year, month) %>%
  summarise(
    sal_mean = mean(sal_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    sal_min  = mean(sal_min,  na.rm = TRUE),
    sal_max  = mean(sal_max,  na.rm = TRUE),
    n_days   = n(),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Require at least 10 days for a valid monthly summary
 filter(n_days >= 10)

cat("\n--- Monthly salinity aggregation ---\n")
cat("Station-months:", nrow(salt_monthly), "\n")

# ── 2. Distance lookup: beach to salinity stations ─────────────────────────
st_sal <- salt_monthly %>%
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) %>%
  distinct(station, latitude, longitude)

bsd_sal <- bc %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    ds = list(st_sal %>% mutate(d = hav(blat, blon, latitude, longitude)))
  ) %>%
  unnest(ds) %>%
  select(beach, station, d) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("\n--- Salinity station distances to beaches ---\n")
bsd_sal %>%
  mutate(d = round(d, 1)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = station, values_from = d) %>%
  print()

# ── 3. Identify which beaches have at least one station within range ───────
beaches_with_sal <- bsd_sal %>%
  filter(d <= sal_max_dist) %>%
  distinct(beach) %>%
  pull(beach)

beaches_without_sal <- setdiff(beach_order, beaches_with_sal)

cat("\n--- Salinity coverage at", sal_max_dist, "km radius ---\n")
cat("Beaches WITH  local salinity:", paste(beaches_with_sal, collapse = ", "), "\n")
if (length(beaches_without_sal) > 0) {
  cat("Beaches WITHOUT local salinity:", paste(beaches_without_sal, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  cat("  (nearest station distances for excluded beaches:)\n")
  bsd_sal %>%
    filter(beach %in% beaches_without_sal) %>%
    group_by(beach) %>%
    summarise(nearest_station = station[which.min(d)],
              nearest_km = round(min(d), 1),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    print()
}

# ── 4. IDW blending (only for beaches with stations in range) ─────────────
aym_sal <- salt_monthly %>% distinct(year, month)

if (length(beaches_with_sal) > 0) {
  wi_sal <- bc %>%
    filter(beach %in% beaches_with_sal) %>%
    select(beach) %>%
    cross_join(aym_sal) %>%
    mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month)) %>%
    left_join(bsd_sal, by = "beach", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    left_join(
      salt_monthly %>% select(station, year, month, sal_mean, sal_min, sal_max),
      by = c("station", "year", "month"), relationship = "many-to-many"
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(sal_mean), d <= sal_max_dist) %>%
    mutate(w = 1 / d ^ idwp) %>%
    group_by(beach, year, month) %>%
    summarise(
      sal      = weighted.mean(sal_mean, w = w),
      sal_lo   = weighted.mean(sal_min,  w = w),
      sal_hi   = weighted.mean(sal_max,  w = w),
      ns_sal   = n(),
      dom_stn_sal = station[which.max(w)],
      .groups  = "drop"
    )
} else {
  # No beaches have salinity coverage — create empty frame
  wi_sal <- tibble(beach = character(), year = integer(), month = integer(),
                   sal = numeric(), sal_lo = numeric(), sal_hi = numeric(),
                   ns_sal = integer(), dom_stn_sal = character())
}

# ── Completeness diagnostic ────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat("\n--- Salinity IDW completeness ---\n")
if (nrow(wi_sal) > 0) {
  wi_sal %>%
    group_by(beach) %>%
    summarise(
      n_months   = n(),
      year_range = paste(min(year), max(year), sep = "–"),
      avg_stns   = round(mean(ns_sal), 1),
      dom_stn    = names(which.max(table(dom_stn_sal))),
      min_dist   = round(min(bsd_sal$d[bsd_sal$beach == first(beach) &
                                        bsd_sal$d <= sal_max_dist]), 1),
      .groups    = "drop"
    ) %>%
    print()
} else {
  cat("No beaches have salinity stations within", sal_max_dist, "km\n")
}

if (length(beaches_without_sal) > 0) {
  cat("\nNote:", paste(beaches_without_sal, collapse = " and "),
      "will have NA for all salinity predictors.\n",
      "Add closer buoy data to DailySalt.xlsx to enable salinity at these beaches.\n")
}
```


## 4e. Columbia River discharge (monthly aggregation)

```{r}
# ── Aggregate daily discharge to monthly means ────────────────────────────
# Columbia River discharge is coast-wide (same for all beaches) but its
# influence varies geographically — strongest at Long Beach (nearest the
# plume), diminishing northward.

if (!is.null(cr_discharge)) {
  discharge_monthly <- cr_discharge %>%
    mutate(month = as.numeric(.data$month)) %>%
    group_by(year, month) %>%
    summarise(
      q_mean = mean(discharge_cms, na.rm = TRUE),
      q_min  = min(discharge_cms,  na.rm = TRUE),
      q_max  = max(discharge_cms,  na.rm = TRUE),
      n_days = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(n_days >= 15)  # require ≥15 days for valid monthly mean
  
  cat("\n--- Monthly discharge aggregation ---\n")
  cat("Station-months:", nrow(discharge_monthly), "\n")
  cat("Year range:", min(discharge_monthly$year), "–", max(discharge_monthly$year), "\n")
} else {
  discharge_monthly <- NULL
  cat("\n--- Discharge data unavailable — skipping discharge predictor ---\n")
}
```

## 5a. Recruitment time series

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=12}
# ── Recruitment time series: pre-recruits and recruits by beach over time ──
# Shows the full 1997–2025 survey record. Helps identify major recruitment
# events, failures, and whether patterns are synchronous across beaches.

rec_ts_plot <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    sy    = as.integer(str_extract(season, "^[0-9]{4}")),
    beach = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  select(beach, sy, pre_recruits, recruits) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(pre_recruits, recruits),
               names_to = "class", values_to = "abundance") %>%
  mutate(class = recode(class,
                        pre_recruits = "Pre-recruits (< 76 mm)",
                        recruits     = "Recruits (≥ 76 mm)"))

p_rec_ts <- rec_ts_plot %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = sy, y = abundance, color = class)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Pre-recruits (< 76 mm)" = "steelblue",
                                 "Recruits (≥ 76 mm)"     = "firebrick")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  facet_wrap(~beach, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x     = "Survey year",
       y     = "Abundance (clams per survey)",
       title = "Razor clam recruitment time series (1997–2025)",
       subtitle = "Pre-recruits (< 76 mm, blue) and recruits (≥ 76 mm, red) at each beach",
       color = NULL) +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"))

print(p_rec_ts)
if (save_summary) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "summary", "recruitment_timeseries.png"),
         plot = p_rec_ts, width = 14, height = 12, dpi = 300)
}
```

## 5b. Columbia River discharge climatology

```{r fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
# ── Discharge seasonal climatology (spaghetti style) ─────────────────────
# Same visualization as temperature: faint lines per year, bold mean overlay.
# Shows the spring freshet (May–Jun peak), fall/winter low, and interannual
# variability in flow timing and magnitude.

if (!is.null(discharge_monthly) && use_discharge) {
  q_clim <- discharge_monthly %>%
    group_by(month) %>%
    summarise(mean_q = mean(q_mean, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  
  p_discharge_clim <- ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = discharge_monthly,
              aes(x = month, y = q_mean, group = year),
              alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.4, color = "steelblue") +
    geom_line(data = q_clim,
              aes(x = month, y = mean_q),
              linewidth = 1.8, color = "navy") +
    geom_point(data = q_clim,
               aes(x = month, y = mean_q),
               size = 3, color = "navy") +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 4.5, xmax = 8.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "gold", alpha = 0.10) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
    labs(x        = "Month",
         y        = expression("Mean discharge (m"^3*"/s)"),
         title    = "Columbia River discharge climatology (The Dalles, USGS 14105700)",
         subtitle = "Faint lines = individual years; bold line = long-term average") +
    my_theme
  
  print(p_discharge_clim)
  if (save_climatology) {
    ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "climatology", "seasonal_climatology_discharge.png"),
           plot = p_discharge_clim, width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
  }
} else {
  cat("Discharge climatology plot skipped — data unavailable or use_discharge = FALSE\n")
}
```

## 5c. Temperature and salinity climatology (spaghetti style)

```{r fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
# ── Seasonal climatology: individual year lines (muted) + bold average ─────
# "Spaghetti plot" approach: every year is drawn as a faint line in a muted
# shade of the beach's color. The overall mean across years is drawn as a bold
# line in the beach's true color. All beaches share the same y-axis so
# cross-beach thermal differences are immediately visible.

# Assign a consistent color per beach (Dark2 palette, ordered N to S)
beach_colors <- setNames(
  RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(max(3, length(beach_order)), "Dark2")[seq_along(beach_order)],
  beach_order
)

# ── Function to make a climatology spaghetti plot for a given temp metric ──
plot_clim_spaghetti <- function(metric_col, metric_label, title_suffix) {
  # Prepare yearly data
  yearly_dat <- wi %>%
    mutate(beach = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE)) %>%
    rename(temp_val = !!sym(metric_col))
  
  # Compute the climatology (mean across years)
  clim_dat <- yearly_dat %>%
    group_by(beach, month) %>%
    summarise(mean_t = mean(temp_val, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  
  # Shared y-axis limits across all beaches
  y_range <- range(c(yearly_dat$temp_val, clim_dat$mean_t), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  p <- ggplot() +
    # Individual year lines: muted color, thin, semi-transparent
    geom_line(data = yearly_dat,
              aes(x = month, y = temp_val, group = interaction(beach, year),
                  color = beach),
              alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.4) +
    # Bold average line per beach
    geom_line(data = clim_dat,
              aes(x = month, y = mean_t, color = beach, group = beach),
              linewidth = 1.5) +
    geom_point(data = clim_dat,
               aes(x = month, y = mean_t, color = beach),
               size = 2.5) +
    # Shade biologically important May–Aug window
    annotate("rect", xmin = 4.5, xmax = 8.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "gold", alpha = 0.10) +
    annotate("text", x = 6.5, y = y_range[1] + 0.5,
             label = "May–Aug\n(spawning–settlement)",
             size = 3.5, color = "goldenrod4", fontface = "italic") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
    scale_color_manual(values = beach_colors, name = "Beach (N → S)") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = y_range + c(-0.5, 0.5)) +
    labs(x     = "Month",
         y     = paste0(metric_label, " water temperature (°C)"),
         title = paste("Seasonal temperature climatology —", title_suffix),
         subtitle = "Faint lines = individual years; bold lines = long-term average") +
    my_theme +
    theme(legend.position = "right")
  
  return(p)
}

# Generate and save climatology plots (min, max, salinity)
p_clim_min  <- plot_clim_spaghetti("at_min", "Minimum", "Min temp — upwelling proxy")
p_clim_max  <- plot_clim_spaghetti("at_max", "Maximum", "Max temp — thermal stress proxy")

print(p_clim_min)
print(p_clim_max)

if (save_climatology) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "climatology", "seasonal_climatology_min_temp.png"),
         plot = p_clim_min,  width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "climatology", "seasonal_climatology_max_temp.png"),
         plot = p_clim_max,  width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
}

# ── Salinity climatology spaghetti plot ──────────────────────────────────
if (nrow(wi_sal) > 0) {
  sal_yearly <- wi_sal %>%
    mutate(beach = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE))
  
  sal_clim <- sal_yearly %>%
    group_by(beach, month) %>%
    summarise(mean_sal = mean(sal, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  
  y_sal_range <- range(c(sal_yearly$sal, sal_clim$mean_sal), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  sal_subtitle <- paste0("Beaches within ", sal_max_dist, " km of salinity buoys: ",
                          paste(beaches_with_sal, collapse = ", "))
  
  p_clim_sal <- ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = sal_yearly,
              aes(x = month, y = sal, group = interaction(beach, year),
                  color = beach),
              alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_line(data = sal_clim,
              aes(x = month, y = mean_sal, color = beach, group = beach),
              linewidth = 1.5) +
    geom_point(data = sal_clim,
               aes(x = month, y = mean_sal, color = beach),
               size = 2.5) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 4.5, xmax = 8.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "gold", alpha = 0.10) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
    scale_color_manual(values = beach_colors, name = "Beach (N → S)") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = y_sal_range + c(-0.5, 0.5)) +
    labs(x     = "Month",
         y     = "IDW-blended salinity (PSU)",
         title = "Seasonal salinity climatology (2014–2025)",
         subtitle = sal_subtitle) +
    my_theme +
    theme(legend.position = "right")
  
  print(p_clim_sal)
  if (save_climatology) {
    ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "climatology", "seasonal_climatology_salinity.png"),
           plot = p_clim_sal, width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
  }
} else {
  cat("Salinity climatology plot skipped — no beaches within", sal_max_dist, "km of buoys\n")
}
```
