## 19a. Generalized Lag Profile — "Which environmental factor matters, and when?"

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# For each metric × lag, average the |r| across all beaches and seasonal
# windows to produce a generalized "lag response curve." This shows the
# overall temporal footprint of each environmental factor on recruitment.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── Version A: Separate panels for pre-recruits and recruits ────────────
lag_profile <- cor_all %>%
  filter(timescale == "monthly") %>%
  select(beach, lag, metric, window, r_pre, r_rec) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(r_pre, r_rec),
               names_to = "recruit_type", values_to = "r") %>%
  mutate(recruit_type = recode(recruit_type,
                                r_pre = "Pre-recruits (< 76 mm)",
                                r_rec = "Recruits (≥ 76 mm)")) %>%
  group_by(metric, lag, recruit_type) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_r   = mean(r, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_r     = sd(r, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(r))),
    mean_abs = mean(abs(r), na.rm = TRUE),
    n        = sum(!is.na(r)),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = metric_levels))

# Color palette for metrics
metric_colors <- c(
  Min       = "#2166AC",
  Max       = "#B2182B",
  CUTI      = "#762A83",
  BEUTI     = "#1B7837",
  Salinity  = "#E08214",
  Discharge = "#542788"
)
active_metric_colors <- metric_colors[intersect(names(metric_colors), metric_levels)]

p_lagprofile_A <- lag_profile %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lag, y = mean_r, color = metric, fill = metric)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey50") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean_r - se_r, ymax = mean_r + se_r),
              alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = active_metric_colors, name = "Environmental factor") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = active_metric_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = lag_range,
                     labels = paste0("Lag ", lag_range, "\n(",
                                     c("same year", "1 yr prior", "2 yr prior",
                                       "3 yr prior", "4 yr prior", "5 yr prior")[1:length(lag_range)],
                                     ")")) +
  facet_wrap(~recruit_type) +
  labs(x     = NULL,
       y     = "Mean Pearson r (± SE across beaches & windows)",
       title = "Generalized lag response: how do environmental conditions relate to future clam abundance?",
       subtitle = "Averaged across all 5 beaches and 5 seasonal windows | Positive r = higher values → more clams") +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position  = "right",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 10))

print(p_lagprofile_A)
if (save_synthesis) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "synthesis", "lag_profile_mean_r.png"),
         plot = p_lagprofile_A, width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 300)
}
```

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# ── Version B: Absolute correlation strength — "signal strength by lag" ──
# Uses mean |r| so positive and negative effects don't cancel out.
# Better for answering: "at which lag does each factor have the most
# predictive power, regardless of direction?"

p_lagprofile_B <- lag_profile %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lag, y = mean_abs, color = metric)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.3) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = active_metric_colors, name = "Environmental factor") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = lag_range) +
  facet_wrap(~recruit_type) +
  labs(x     = "Lag (years prior to survey)",
       y     = "Mean |r| across beaches & windows",
       title = "Predictive signal strength by lag year",
       subtitle = "Higher values = stronger average association regardless of direction") +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position  = "right",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"))

print(p_lagprofile_B)
if (save_synthesis) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "synthesis", "lag_profile_abs_r.png"),
         plot = p_lagprofile_B, width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 300)
}
```

## 19b. Life History Lag Diagram — "From ocean to fishery"

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=10}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# A visual "timeline" showing which lags matter for recruits, arranged
# to tell the life-history story. For each metric, plot the mean
# correlation with RECRUIT abundance at each lag, with ALL individual
# beach values shown as semi-transparent lines behind the mean.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Life-history stage labels for recruits (≥ 76 mm at survey = 1–5+ yr old, WA growth model)
lag_life_labels <- c(
  "Lag 0\nCurrent-year\nsurvival (survey year)",
  "Lag 1\nJuvenile spawning\nsignal (1 yr prior)",
  "Lag 2\nSub-adult/Adult\nspawning (2 yr prior)",
  "Lag 3\nAdult cohort\nspawning (3 yr prior)",
  "Lag 4\nAdult cohort\nspawning (4 yr prior)",
  "Lag 5\nOldest adult cohort\nspawning (5 yr prior)"
)

recruit_by_lag <- cor_all %>%
  filter(timescale == "monthly") %>%
  # Average across seasonal windows for each beach × metric × lag
  group_by(beach, lag, metric) %>%
  summarise(r = mean(r_rec, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    metric = factor(metric, levels = metric_levels),
    beach  = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE)
  )

# Grand mean across beaches
recruit_mean <- recruit_by_lag %>%
  group_by(metric, lag) %>%
  summarise(r = mean(r, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

p_lifehistory <- ggplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey50") +
  # Individual beach lines (faint)
  geom_line(data = recruit_by_lag,
            aes(x = lag, y = r, group = beach, color = metric),
            alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = recruit_by_lag,
             aes(x = lag, y = r, group = beach, color = metric),
             alpha = 0.25, size = 1.5) +
  # Grand mean (bold)
  geom_line(data = recruit_mean,
            aes(x = lag, y = r, color = metric),
            linewidth = 1.8) +
  geom_point(data = recruit_mean,
             aes(x = lag, y = r, color = metric),
             size = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = active_metric_colors, name = "Environmental\nfactor") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = lag_range,
                     labels = lag_life_labels[1:length(lag_range)]) +
  annotate("segment", x = 5.3, xend = -0.3, y = -Inf, yend = -Inf,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), type = "closed"),
           color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = 2.5, y = -Inf, label = "← Time flows forward to survey →",
           vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, color = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  labs(x     = NULL,
       y     = "Mean Pearson r with recruit abundance",
       title = "From ocean conditions to harvestable clams: the lag-life-history pathway",
       subtitle = paste0("Bold lines = mean across all beaches | Faint lines = individual beaches\n",
                         "Recruits (≥ 76 mm) surveyed in summer → harvested in fall–spring fishery")) +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.text.x     = element_text(size = 9, lineheight = 0.9))

print(p_lifehistory)
if (save_synthesis) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "synthesis", "life_history_lag_recruits.png"),
         plot = p_lifehistory, width = 16, height = 10, dpi = 300)
}
```

## 19c. North-to-South Gradient — "Geography shapes the response"

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Show how the strength and direction of each environmental factor's
# best-lag correlation varies from Kalaloch (N) to Long Beach (S).
# Uses best lag per beach × metric for recruit abundance.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Best-lag r for recruits per beach × metric
n2s_best <- cor_all %>%
  filter(timescale == "monthly") %>%
  group_by(beach, metric, window) %>%
  slice_max(abs(r_rec), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Now get best across windows
  group_by(beach, metric) %>%
  slice_max(abs(r_rec), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    sig = ifelse(p_rec < 0.05, "p < 0.05", "n.s."),
    metric = factor(metric, levels = metric_levels),
    beach  = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE)
  )

p_n2s <- n2s_best %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = beach, y = r_rec, fill = metric, alpha = sig)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey50") +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7,
           color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = active_metric_colors, name = "Environmental factor") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("p < 0.05" = 1, "n.s." = 0.35),
                     name = "Significance") +
  labs(x     = "Beach (North → South)",
       y     = "Best-lag Pearson r with recruit abundance",
       title = "Environmental influence on recruits varies along the coast",
       subtitle = paste0("Bar height = strongest correlation at optimal lag | ",
                         "Faded bars = not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.05)")) +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.text.x     = element_text(size = 12))

print(p_n2s)
if (save_synthesis) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "synthesis", "n_to_s_best_lag_recruits.png"),
         plot = p_n2s, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 300)
}
```

## 19d. Lagged Time Series Overlay — "The smoking gun"

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=16}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# For each beach, overlay the best environmental predictor (time-shifted
# by its optimal lag) against the actual recruit time series. When the
# two lines track each other, it's the most intuitive visual proof of the
# environmental–recruitment link.
#
# Uses Z-scores (standard deviations from mean) so different units can
# share the same axis.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Find the single best predictor for recruits at each beach (across all
# metrics, windows, and lags)
best_pred_per_beach <- cor_all %>%
  filter(timescale == "monthly") %>%
  group_by(beach) %>%
  slice_max(abs(r_rec), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(beach, temp_var, window, metric, lag, r_rec, p_rec, sig_rec)

cat("\n--- Best single predictor for recruits per beach ---\n")
best_pred_per_beach %>%
  mutate(r_rec = round(r_rec, 3)) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# Build lagged overlay data
overlay_list <- list()

for (i in 1:nrow(best_pred_per_beach)) {
  bch  <- best_pred_per_beach$beach[i]
  tvar <- best_pred_per_beach$temp_var[i]
  lg   <- best_pred_per_beach$lag[i]
  met  <- best_pred_per_beach$metric[i]
  win  <- best_pred_per_beach$window[i]
  rval <- round(best_pred_per_beach$r_rec[i], 2)
  sig  <- best_pred_per_beach$sig_rec[i]
  
  # Recruitment time series
  rec_bch <- rec_ts %>%
    filter(beach == bch) %>%
    select(sy, recruits) %>%
    mutate(z_recruits = scale(recruits)[,1])
  
  # Predictor time series at the optimal lag
  pred_bch <- ti_monthly %>%
    filter(beach == bch) %>%
    select(year, all_of(tvar)) %>%
    rename(pred_val = !!tvar) %>%
    mutate(
      sy     = year + lg,   # shift forward by lag
      z_pred = scale(pred_val)[,1]
    )
  
  overlay_list[[i]] <- rec_bch %>%
    left_join(pred_bch %>% select(sy, z_pred, pred_val), by = "sy") %>%
    mutate(
      beach     = bch,
      metric    = met,
      window    = win,
      lag       = lg,
      label     = paste0(met, " ", win, " (L", lg, ") r=", rval, sig)
    )
}

overlay_dat <- bind_rows(overlay_list) %>%
  mutate(beach = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE))

p_overlay <- overlay_dat %>%
  select(beach, sy, z_recruits, z_pred, label) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(z_recruits, z_pred),
               names_to = "series", values_to = "z_score") %>%
  mutate(series = recode(series,
                          z_recruits = "Recruit abundance",
                          z_pred     = "Environmental predictor")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = sy, y = z_score, color = series, linewidth = series)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey60") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = . %>% filter(series == "Recruit abundance"),
             size = 1.8, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Recruit abundance"       = "black",
                                 "Environmental predictor" = "#E31A1C"),
                     name = NULL) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c("Recruit abundance" = 1.2,
                                     "Environmental predictor" = 1.0),
                         guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~beach + label, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y",
             labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 80)) +
  labs(x     = "Survey year",
       y     = "Standardized value (Z-score)",
       title = "Best environmental predictor tracks recruit abundance when time-shifted",
       subtitle = "Red line = environmental predictor shifted forward by optimal lag | Black = actual recruit counts") +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 10))

print(p_overlay)
if (save_synthesis) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "synthesis", "lagged_overlay_best_predictor.png"),
         plot = p_overlay, width = 14, height = 16, dpi = 300)
}
```

## 19e. BEUTI Focus — "Upwelling drives the coast"

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=14}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# If BEUTI is active, produce a focused overlay of BEUTI (the dominant
# recruit predictor at mid-coast beaches) against recruit abundance.
# Uses a fixed biologically motivated window (larval+settlement, Jun–Aug)
# at lags 2–5 to show the spawning-to-harvest pipeline.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

if (use_beuti) {
  
  # Find the best BEUTI lag per beach (for recruits)
  beuti_best <- cor_all %>%
    filter(timescale == "monthly", metric == "BEUTI") %>%
    group_by(beach) %>%
    slice_max(abs(r_rec), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(beach, temp_var, window, lag, r_rec, p_rec, sig_rec)
  
  cat("\n--- Best BEUTI lag per beach (recruits) ---\n")
  beuti_best %>% mutate(r_rec = round(r_rec, 3)) %>% print()
  
  beuti_overlay <- map_dfr(1:nrow(beuti_best), function(i) {
    bch  <- beuti_best$beach[i]
    tvar <- beuti_best$temp_var[i]
    lg   <- beuti_best$lag[i]
    rval <- round(beuti_best$r_rec[i], 2)
    sig  <- beuti_best$sig_rec[i]
    win  <- beuti_best$window[i]
    
    rec_bch <- rec_ts %>%
      filter(beach == bch) %>%
      select(sy, recruits) %>%
      mutate(z_recruits = scale(recruits)[,1])
    
    pred_bch <- ti_monthly %>%
      filter(beach == bch) %>%
      select(year, all_of(tvar)) %>%
      rename(pred_val = !!tvar) %>%
      mutate(sy = year + lg, z_beuti = scale(pred_val)[,1])
    
    rec_bch %>%
      left_join(pred_bch %>% select(sy, z_beuti), by = "sy") %>%
      mutate(
        beach = bch,
        lag   = lg,
        label = paste0(bch, " — BEUTI ", win, " (Lag ", lg, ")  r = ", rval, sig)
      )
  }) %>%
    mutate(beach = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE))
  
  # Flip BEUTI sign if correlation is negative (so visual alignment makes sense)
  beuti_overlay <- beuti_overlay %>%
    left_join(beuti_best %>% select(beach, r_rec), by = "beach") %>%
    mutate(z_beuti_aligned = ifelse(r_rec < 0, -z_beuti, z_beuti))
  
  p_beuti_focus <- beuti_overlay %>%
    select(beach, sy, z_recruits, z_beuti_aligned, label) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(z_recruits, z_beuti_aligned),
                 names_to = "series", values_to = "z") %>%
    mutate(series = recode(series,
                            z_recruits       = "Recruit abundance",
                            z_beuti_aligned  = "BEUTI (lagged, aligned)")) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = sy, y = z, color = series, linewidth = series)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey60") +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(data = . %>% filter(series == "Recruit abundance"),
               size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Recruit abundance"      = "black",
                                   "BEUTI (lagged, aligned)" = "#1B7837"),
                       name = NULL) +
    scale_linewidth_manual(values = c("Recruit abundance" = 1.3,
                                       "BEUTI (lagged, aligned)" = 1.0),
                           guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~label, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x     = "Survey year (summer stock assessment → fall/spring fishery)",
         y     = "Standardized value (Z-score)",
         title = "Biologically effective upwelling (BEUTI) predicts recruit abundance",
         subtitle = paste0("Green = BEUTI shifted forward by optimal lag | ",
                          "Black = recruits counted in summer survey\n",
                          "Strong BEUTI during larval/settlement phase → more harvestable clams years later")) +
    my_theme +
    theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#E5F5E0", color = "black"),
          strip.text       = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"))
  
  print(p_beuti_focus)
  if (save_synthesis) {
    ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "synthesis", "beuti_overlay_recruits.png"),
           plot = p_beuti_focus, width = 14, height = 14, dpi = 300)

} else {
```

## 19f. Cross-Beach Correlation Heatstrip — "The big picture in one panel"

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=9}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# A compact summary: beaches (N→S) on y-axis, lags on x-axis, fill = r,
# separate panels per metric. Shows the full correlation landscape for
# recruits in a single figure.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

heatstrip_dat <- cor_all %>%
  filter(timescale == "monthly") %>%
  # Average across seasonal windows per beach × metric × lag
  group_by(beach, metric, lag) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_r = mean(r_rec, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_r  = r_rec[which.max(abs(r_rec))],
    best_p = p_rec[which.max(abs(r_rec))],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = factor(metric, levels = metric_levels),
    beach  = factor(beach, levels = rev(beach_order), ordered = TRUE),
    sig    = best_p < 0.05
  )

p_heatstrip <- heatstrip_dat %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(lag), y = beach, fill = mean_r)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", mean_r)),
            size = 3, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-0.65, 0.65),
                       name = "Mean r") +
  facet_wrap(~metric, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x     = "Lag (years prior to summer survey)",
       y     = "Beach (South → North)",
       title = "Environmental–recruit correlations across the full lag × beach × metric landscape",
       subtitle = "Cell values = mean Pearson r with recruit abundance, averaged across seasonal windows") +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 11))

print(p_heatstrip)
if (save_synthesis) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "synthesis", "heatstrip_beach_lag_metric.png"),
         plot = p_heatstrip, width = 16, height = 9, dpi = 300)
}
```

## 19g. Environmental Timeline Dashboard — "The year in the ocean"

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=18}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Stacked standardized time series of all active environmental factors
# at a representative beach, alongside the recruitment time series.
# Shows how different factors co-vary over the 1997–2025 record.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Use spawn window (May–Jun) as representative seasonal index
spawn_vars <- tv_all[grepl("spawn", tv_all)]

if (length(spawn_vars) > 0) {
  
  # Build long-format environmental data for all beaches
  env_ts <- ti_monthly %>%
    select(beach, year, all_of(spawn_vars)) %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(spawn_vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(metric = metric_labels[variable]) %>%
    group_by(beach, metric) %>%
    mutate(z_value = scale(value)[,1]) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      beach  = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE),
      metric = factor(metric, levels = metric_levels)
    )
  
  # Z-scored recruitment
  rec_z <- rec_ts %>%
    mutate(
      z_rec = scale(recruits)[,1],
      z_pre = scale(pre_recruits)[,1]
    ) %>%
    select(beach, sy, z_rec, z_pre)
  
  # Pick the middle beach for the main dashboard
  mid_beach <- beach_order[ceiling(length(beach_order) / 2)]
  
  env_mid <- env_ts %>% filter(beach == mid_beach)
  rec_mid <- rec_z %>% filter(beach == mid_beach)
  
  # Build individual panels
  env_panels <- env_mid %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = year, y = z_value, color = metric)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey60") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = active_metric_colors, guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~metric, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y", strip.position = "left") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
         title = paste0("Environmental conditions at ", mid_beach,
                        " — Spawn window (May–Jun)"),
         subtitle = "Standardized values (Z-scores): above zero = above average") +
    my_theme +
    theme(strip.background  = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
          strip.text        = element_text(size = 10),
          strip.placement   = "outside",
          axis.text.x       = element_blank())
  
  rec_panel <- rec_mid %>%
    pivot_longer(c(z_rec, z_pre), names_to = "class", values_to = "z") %>%
    mutate(class = recode(class,
                           z_rec = "Recruits (≥ 76 mm)",
                           z_pre = "Pre-recruits (< 76 mm)")) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = sy, y = z, color = class)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey60") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Recruits (≥ 76 mm)"     = "firebrick",
                                   "Pre-recruits (< 76 mm)" = "steelblue"),
                       name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Z-score",
         subtitle = paste0("Clam abundance at ", mid_beach, " (summer survey)")) +
    my_theme +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  p_dashboard <- env_panels / rec_panel +
    plot_layout(heights = c(4, 1.5)) +
    plot_annotation(
      title    = "Environmental conditions and recruitment: a 25-year record",
      subtitle = paste0("Do you see years where multiple factors align with high/low recruitment?\n",
                        "Remember: environmental effects are lagged 2–5 years before appearing as recruits"),
      theme    = theme(plot.title    = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
                       plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "grey30"))
    )
  
  print(p_dashboard)
  if (save_synthesis) {
    ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "synthesis",
                     paste0("env_dashboard_", gsub(" ", "_", tolower(mid_beach)), ".png")),
           plot = p_dashboard, width = 16, height = 18, dpi = 300)
  }
}
```

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

## 19i. Cohort Trace — "What made a good (or bad) year?"

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=10}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Pick the highest and lowest recruitment years at a representative beach
# and "trace back" through the lagged environmental conditions. Shows
# a paired comparison: what was different in the ocean 2–5 years before
# a boom vs a bust?
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Use spawn window indices at the mid-coast beach
trace_beach <- beach_order[ceiling(length(beach_order) / 2)]

rec_trace <- rec_ts %>%
  filter(beach == trace_beach, !is.na(recruits)) %>%
  arrange(desc(recruits))

top_yr    <- rec_trace$sy[1]
bottom_yr <- rec_trace$sy[nrow(rec_trace)]

cat("\n--- Cohort trace at", trace_beach, "---\n")
cat("Best recruitment year:", top_yr, "(", rec_trace$recruits[1], "recruits)\n")
cat("Worst recruitment year:", bottom_yr, "(", rec_trace$recruits[nrow(rec_trace)], "recruits)\n")

# Build environmental lookback for both years
trace_dat <- map_dfr(lag_range, function(lg) {
  env_yr <- ti_monthly %>%
    filter(beach == trace_beach) %>%
    select(year, all_of(spawn_vars)) %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(spawn_vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(metric = metric_labels[variable])
  
  bind_rows(
    env_yr %>% filter(.data$year == top_yr - lg) %>%
      mutate(cohort = paste0("Best: ", top_yr, " (", rec_trace$recruits[1], " recruits)"),
             lag = lg, env_year = top_yr - lg),
    env_yr %>% filter(.data$year == bottom_yr - lg) %>%
      mutate(cohort = paste0("Worst: ", bottom_yr, " (", rec_trace$recruits[nrow(rec_trace)], " recruits)"),
             lag = lg, env_year = bottom_yr - lg)
  )
}) %>%
  # Z-score within each metric for comparability
  group_by(metric) %>%
  mutate(z_value = (value - mean(value, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = metric_levels))

p_cohort <- trace_dat %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lag, y = z_value, color = cohort, group = cohort)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.3) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(setNames("#B2182B", paste0("Best: ", top_yr, " (", rec_trace$recruits[1], " recruits)")),
                                 setNames("#2166AC", paste0("Worst: ", bottom_yr, " (", rec_trace$recruits[nrow(rec_trace)], " recruits)"))),
                     name = "Survey year") +
  scale_x_reverse(breaks = lag_range,
                  labels = paste0("Lag ", lag_range, "\n(", 
                                  c("survey yr", "1 yr prior", "2 yr prior",
                                    "3 yr prior", "4 yr prior", "5 yr prior")[1:length(lag_range)],
                                  ")")) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x     = "Looking backward from survey year ←",
       y     = "Environmental condition (Z-score)",
       title = paste0("What made a boom vs bust year at ", trace_beach, "?"),
       subtitle = paste0("Tracing environmental conditions backward from the best and worst recruit survey years\n",
                         "Spawn window (May–Jun) indices | Z-score > 0 = above long-term average")) +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 9, lineheight = 0.9))

print(p_cohort)
if (save_synthesis) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "synthesis",
                   paste0("cohort_trace_", gsub(" ", "_", tolower(trace_beach)), ".png")),
         plot = p_cohort, width = 16, height = 10, dpi = 300)
}
```

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SECTION 20: WINDOW-RESOLVED SEASONAL TIMING ANALYSIS
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# Section 19 averaged across seasonal windows to show generalized lag patterns.
# This section PRESERVES the seasonal window dimension to answer:
#   "WHEN in the lag year do conditions matter?"
#
# The 5 seasonal windows map to specific months within each lag year:
#   Spring (Mar–May) — spring transition, early upwelling
#   Spawn  (May–Jun) — razor clam spawning period
#   Larval (Jun–Jul) — peak planktonic larval phase
#   Settle (Jul–Aug) — larval settlement to benthos
#   Growth (Sep–Oct) — post-settlement juvenile growth
#
# Each window at each lag corresponds to a specific life-history stage,
# and the combination reveals the precise oceanographic bottleneck.

```{r}
dir.create(file.path(folder_name, "windows"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

cat("\n═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("  SECTION 20: Window-Resolved Seasonal Timing Analysis\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")

# ── Shared objects used throughout Section 20 ────────────────────────────
# Window ordering (chronological within a year)
window_order <- c("Spring", "Spawn", "Larval", "Settle", "Growth")
window_months <- c(Spring = "Mar–May", Spawn = "May–Jun", Larval = "Jun–Jul",
                   Settle = "Jul–Aug", Growth = "Sep–Oct")

# Color palette for metrics (reuse from Section 19 if available, else define)
if (!exists("active_metric_colors")) {
  metric_colors <- c(Min = "#2166AC", Max = "#B2182B", CUTI = "#762A83",
                     BEUTI = "#1B7837", Salinity = "#E08214", Discharge = "#542788")
  active_metric_colors <- metric_colors[intersect(names(metric_colors), metric_levels)]
}

# Prepare the master window-resolved dataset from cor_all
wr <- cor_all %>%
  filter(timescale == "monthly") %>%
  mutate(
    window = factor(window, levels = window_order, ordered = TRUE),
    metric = factor(metric, levels = metric_levels),
    beach  = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE)
  )
```

## 20a. Seasonal Cascade — "5 years of ocean history, one continuous timeline"

```{r fig.width=18, fig.height=14}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# A continuous x-axis concatenates all 30 window×lag combinations
# chronologically: from Growth at lag 5 (the oldest conditions) through
# Spring at lag 0 (most recent). Each point on the x-axis is a specific
# 2-month window in a specific lag year. Reading left to right traces
# the full environmental history of a recruit cohort.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Build a continuous cascade index:
# Lag 5 Growth → Lag 5 Settle → ... → Lag 5 Spring → Lag 4 Growth → ... → Lag 0 Spring
# Reversed so oldest conditions are on the LEFT (time flows right → survey)
cascade <- wr %>%
  mutate(
    # Position: each lag-window combo gets a unique x position
    # Lag 5 is the earliest (leftmost), within each lag, Growth is earliest
    # (Sep-Oct of that year precedes the next year's Spring)
    # BUT within a single year: Spring→Spawn→Larval→Settle→Growth is chronological
    win_num  = as.integer(window),  # 1=Spring...5=Growth
    cascade_x = (max_lag - lag) * 5 + win_num,
    # Short labels for x-axis ticks
    cascade_label = paste0(substr(as.character(window), 1, 2), "\nL", lag)
  )

# --- RECRUITS version ---
p_cascade_rec <- cascade %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = cascade_x, y = r_rec, color = metric)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey50") +
  # Vertical separators between lag years
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(5.5, 25.5, by = 5),
             linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(size = ifelse(p_rec < 0.05, 3, 1.5),
                 shape = ifelse(p_rec < 0.05, 19, 1)),
             alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_size_identity() +
  scale_shape_identity() +
  scale_color_manual(values = active_metric_colors, name = "Environmental\nfactor") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = cascade %>% distinct(cascade_x, cascade_label) %>%
      arrange(cascade_x) %>% pull(cascade_x),
    labels = cascade %>% distinct(cascade_x, cascade_label) %>%
      arrange(cascade_x) %>% pull(cascade_label),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ .,
      breaks = seq(3, 28, by = 5),
      labels = paste0("── Lag ", max_lag:0, " (",
                      c("5 yr prior", "4 yr prior", "3 yr prior",
                        "2 yr prior", "1 yr prior", "survey year")[1:(max_lag+1)],
                      ") ──"))
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~beach, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x     = NULL,
       y     = "Pearson r with recruit abundance",
       title = "Seasonal cascade: the full environmental history of a recruit cohort",
       subtitle = paste0("Each point = correlation for a specific 2-month window in a specific lag year\n",
                         "Filled circles = p < 0.05 | Reading left → right traces time from 5 years ago to survey year")) +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position  = "right",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x.bottom = element_text(size = 6, lineheight = 0.85),
        axis.text.x.top    = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", color = "grey30"),
        panel.spacing.y    = unit(0.3, "cm"))

print(p_cascade_rec)
if (save_windows) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "windows", "cascade_recruits.png"),
         plot = p_cascade_rec, width = 18, height = 14, dpi = 300)
}
```

```{r fig.width=18, fig.height=14}
# --- PRE-RECRUITS version ---
p_cascade_pre <- cascade %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = cascade_x, y = r_pre, color = metric)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(5.5, 25.5, by = 5),
             linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(size = ifelse(p_pre < 0.05, 3, 1.5),
```

## 20b. Window × Lag Tile Maps — "The full factorial at a glance"

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=14}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# For each metric, a tile plot: x = lag (0–5), y = seasonal window
# (chronological: Spring at top → Growth at bottom), fill = r.
# Faceted: columns = metrics, rows = beaches (N→S).
# Separate plots for recruits and pre-recruits.
#
# This preserves BOTH the window and lag dimensions — the audience sees
# the exact cell where the correlation peaks.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# --- RECRUITS ---
p_tiles_rec <- wr %>%
  mutate(
    window = factor(window, levels = rev(window_order)),
    sig    = ifelse(p_rec < 0.05, TRUE, FALSE),
    label  = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", r_rec), sig_rec)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(lag), y = window, fill = r_rec)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +

            fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
```

## 20c. Within-Year Timing — "When in the critical year does it matter?"

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=12}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Focus on the biologically critical lag years and show how the
# correlation varies across the 5 seasonal windows WITHIN those years.
# For recruits: lags 2–5 (spawning/settlement signal for adults, WA growth model).
# For pre-recruits: lags 0–1 (settlement for YOY/juveniles).
#
# x = seasonal window (chronological within the lag year),
# y = r, color = lag year, faceted by beach × metric.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# --- RECRUITS: critical lags 2–5 ---
critical_rec <- wr %>%
  filter(lag %in% 2:5) %>%
  mutate(
    lag_label = paste0("Lag ", lag, " (", lag, " yr prior)"),
    sig       = p_rec < 0.05
  )

p_timing_rec <- critical_rec %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = window, y = r_rec, color = factor(lag), group = lag)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = sig), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("2" = "#FEE0B6", "3" = "#FDB863", "4" = "#E08214", "5" = "#B35806"),
                     name = "Lag year",
                     labels = c("2" = "Lag 2 (2 yr prior)",
                                "3" = "Lag 3 (3 yr prior)",
                                "4" = "Lag 4 (4 yr prior)",
                                "5" = "Lag 5 (5 yr prior)")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("TRUE" = 16, "FALSE" = 1),
                     name = "Significant", labels = c("TRUE" = "p < 0.05", "FALSE" = "n.s.")) +
  facet_grid(beach ~ metric) +
  labs(x     = "Seasonal window (chronological within the lag year)",
       y     = "Pearson r with recruit abundance",
       title = "When in the spawning-to-settlement year do ocean conditions matter for recruits?",
       subtitle = paste0("Lags 3–5 span the critical period when harvestable-size clams were spawned, ",
                         "drifted as larvae, and settled\n",
                         "x-axis = month windows within each lag year | Rows = beaches (N → S)")) +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position  = "right",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 9, angle = 35, hjust = 1))

print(p_timing_rec)
if (save_windows) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "windows", "timing_within_year_recruits.png"),
         plot = p_timing_rec, width = 16, height = 12, dpi = 300)
}
```

## 20d. Peak Window Bubble Summary — "The sweet spot for each beach"

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# For each beach × metric, find the single window × lag with the
# highest |r| for recruits. Display as a bubble plot:
#   x = beach (N→S), y = metric
#   Bubble size = |r|, fill = lag year, label = window name
# This is the "one-slide summary" of which seasonal window matters
# where and when.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# --- RECRUITS ---
peak_rec <- wr %>%
  group_by(beach, metric) %>%
  slice_max(abs(r_rec), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    sig      = p_rec < 0.05,
    r_label  = paste0(as.character(window), "\n",
                      sprintf("%.2f", r_rec), sig_rec)
  )

p_bubble_rec <- peak_rec %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = beach, y = metric)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = abs(r_rec), fill = factor(lag)),
             shape = 21, color = "black", stroke = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = peak_rec %>% filter(!sig),
             aes(size = abs(r_rec)),
             shape = 21, fill = "grey85", color = "grey50", stroke = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = r_label), size = 2.5, vjust = -0.1,
            fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.85) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(6, 22), name = "|r|",
                        breaks = c(0.3, 0.5, 0.7)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Best lag\n(years)", option = "turbo",
                       end = 0.9, direction = -1) +
  labs(x     = "Beach (North → South)",
       y     = "Environmental factor",
       title = "The sweet spot: peak window × lag for recruit prediction at each beach",
       subtitle = paste0("Bubble size ∝ |r| | Color = optimal lag year | ",
                         "Labels show window name + r value\n",
                         "Grey bubbles = not significant (p ≥ 0.05)")) +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.text.x     = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 12))

print(p_bubble_rec)
if (save_windows) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "windows", "peak_bubble_recruits.png"),
         plot = p_bubble_rec, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 300)
}
```

## 20e. Window Consistency Across Beaches — "Is it the same season everywhere?"

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=10}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# For each metric at its most relevant lag range, compare the 5 seasonal
# windows across all beaches. This reveals whether "Larval BEUTI at
# lag 5" is universally the best, or whether some beaches respond more
# to "Settle" or "Spring" conditions.
#
# Format: heatmap with x = beach (N→S), y = window, fill = r
# One panel per metric, using the lag that maximizes average |r| across
# beaches for that metric.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# --- RECRUITS: find best overall lag per metric ---
best_lag_per_metric_rec <- wr %>%
  group_by(metric, lag) %>%
  summarise(mean_abs_r = mean(abs(r_rec), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  slice_max(mean_abs_r, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  select(metric, best_lag = lag)

cat("\n--- Best overall lag per metric (recruits) ---\n")
best_lag_per_metric_rec %>% print()

consistency_rec <- wr %>%
  inner_join(best_lag_per_metric_rec, by = "metric") %>%
  filter(lag == best_lag) %>%
  mutate(
    window    = factor(window, levels = rev(window_order)),
    sig       = p_rec < 0.05,
    label     = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", r_rec), sig_rec),
    panel_lab = paste0(metric, " at Lag ", best_lag)
  )

# Factor panel_lab to preserve metric order
consistency_rec <- consistency_rec %>%
  mutate(panel_lab = factor(panel_lab,
    levels = best_lag_per_metric_rec %>%
      mutate(lab = paste0(metric, " at Lag ", best_lag)) %>%
      pull(lab)))

p_consistency_rec <- consistency_rec %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = beach, y = window, fill = r_rec)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_tile(data = . %>% filter(sig),
            fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 3, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-0.8, 0.8), name = "Pearson r") +
  facet_wrap(~panel_lab, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x     = "Beach (North → South)",
       y     = "Seasonal window",
       title = "Which season matters — and is the answer the same at every beach?",
       subtitle = paste0("Each panel shows one environmental factor at its best overall lag for recruits\n",
                         "Black outlines = p < 0.05 | Look for consistent hot/cold rows across beaches")) +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 10, angle = 35, hjust = 1))

print(p_consistency_rec)
if (save_windows) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "windows", "window_consistency_recruits.png"),
         plot = p_consistency_rec, width = 16, height = 10, dpi = 300)
}
```

## 20f. Dominant-Factor Seasonal Fingerprint — "BEUTI and discharge month by month"

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=12}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# For each beach, show the seasonal window profile (x = window, y = r)
# at ALL lags as a set of colored lines for just the dominant factor(s).
# This creates a "fingerprint" showing exactly how the seasonal timing
# of each factor's influence changes with lag.
#
# Cleaner than the full cascade — focuses on the 1–2 most important
# metrics with all their temporal detail.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Pick the two metrics with highest max |r| across all beaches (for recruits)
top2_metrics <- wr %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  summarise(max_abs = max(abs(r_rec), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(max_abs, n = 2) %>%
  pull(metric)

cat("\n--- Top 2 metrics for fingerprint plot:", paste(top2_metrics, collapse = " & "), "---\n")

fingerprint_dat <- wr %>%
  filter(metric %in% top2_metrics) %>%
  mutate(
    lag_label = paste0("Lag ", lag),
    lag_label = factor(lag_label, levels = paste0("Lag ", lag_range))
  )

p_fingerprint_rec <- fingerprint_dat %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = window, y = r_rec, color = lag_label, group = lag)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = ifelse(p_rec < 0.05, "sig", "ns")), size = 2.5) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(sig = 16, ns = 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Lag year", option = "turbo", end = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(beach ~ metric) +
  labs(x     = "Seasonal window within the lag year",
       y     = "Pearson r with recruit abundance",
       title = paste0("Seasonal fingerprint: how ", paste(top2_metrics, collapse = " and "),
                      " timing varies by lag and beach"),
       subtitle = paste0("Each line = one lag year | Filled points = p < 0.05\n",
                         "Peaks reveal the exact months that drive the environmental signal")) +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position  = "right",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 9, angle = 35, hjust = 1))

print(p_fingerprint_rec)
if (save_windows) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "windows", "fingerprint_top2_recruits.png"),
         plot = p_fingerprint_rec, width = 14, height = 12, dpi = 300)
}
```

## 21a. Size-frequency histograms by beach and year

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=20}
# ── Annual size-frequency distributions: stacked histograms per beach ─────
# Each panel = one beach. X-axis = shell length. Rows = survey years.
# Color = age class. This is the foundational view of population structure.

for (bch in beach_order) {
  
  bch_data <- sl_raw %>%
    filter(beach == bch) %>%
    mutate(
      age_class = factor(age_class, levels = age_class_config$age_class),
      survey_year = factor(survey_year)
    )
  
  if (nrow(bch_data) == 0) next
  
  p_hist <- bch_data %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = length_mm, fill = age_class)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0, color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(age_class_config$color, age_class_config$age_class),
                      name = "Age class") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(75, 100, 120), lty = 2, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5) +
    facet_wrap(~survey_year, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x     = "Shell length (mm)",
         y     = "Number of clams",
         title = paste0(bch, " — Size-frequency distributions (1997–2025)"),
         subtitle = "Dashed lines at 75, 100, 120 mm mark size class boundaries") +
    my_theme +
    theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
          strip.text       = element_text(size = 9))
  
  print(p_hist)
  if (save_shell_summary) {
    ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "shell_length",
                     paste0("size_freq_", gsub(" ", "_", tolower(bch)), ".png")),
           plot = p_hist, width = 16, height = 20, dpi = 300)
  }
}
```

## 22d. Cross-beach synchrony: correlation of age class abundances

```{r fig.width=12, fig.height=12}
# ── For each age class, compute pairwise correlations between beaches ─────
# High correlations imply coast-wide forcing; low = local processes dominate.

sync_results <- list()

for (ac_label in age_class_config$short_label) {
  
  wide_ac <- sl_estimated_abundance %>%
    filter(short_label == ac_label) %>%
    select(survey_year, beach, est_abundance) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = beach, values_from = est_abundance) %>%
    select(-survey_year) %>%
    as.matrix()
  
  if (ncol(wide_ac) < 2 || nrow(wide_ac) < 5) next
  
  # Pairwise correlations
  cor_mat <- cor(wide_ac, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  
  sync_results[[ac_label]] <- tibble(
    age_class  = ac_label,
    mean_r     = mean(cor_mat[lower.tri(cor_mat)], na.rm = TRUE),
    min_r      = min(cor_mat[lower.tri(cor_mat)], na.rm = TRUE),
    max_r      = max(cor_mat[lower.tri(cor_mat)], na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

sync_df <- bind_rows(sync_results)
cat("\n--- Cross-beach synchrony by age class ---\n")
print(sync_df)

# Save synchrony results
sync_df_out <- sync_df %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)))
wb_sync <- createWorkbook()
addWorksheet(wb_sync, "Cross_Beach_Synchrony")
writeData(wb_sync, "Cross_Beach_Synchrony", sync_df_out)
saveWorkbook(wb_sync, file.path(folder_name, "excel",
                                 "cross_beach_synchrony_by_age_class.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
```

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SECTION 23: AGE-CLASS-SPECIFIC LAG CORRELATION ANALYSIS
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

```{r}
cat("\n═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("  SECTION 23: Age-Class-Specific Lag Correlation Analysis\n")
cat("  Matching environmental windows to estimated clam age\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
```

## 23a. Build age-class response variable joined to environmental data

```{r}
# ── Create the age-class-specific recruitment base table ──────────────────
# Each row = beach × year × age class with counts + log-transformed response.
# This replaces the simple pre-recruit/recruit split with four age-resolved
# categories, each with a biologically appropriate lag window.

# ── Create the age-class-specific recruitment base table ──────────────────
# Uses ESTIMATED ABUNDANCE (proportion-weighted from beach-wide estimates)
# rather than raw sample counts. This ensures the response variable reflects
# actual population size, not variable sampling effort.
#
# Key distinction:
#   sl_age_counts$n_clams   = raw count of clams measured in transects (sample)
#   sl_estimated_abundance$est_abundance = beach-wide estimate (density × area)
#
# The log-transformed estimated abundance is the response for all modeling.

rec_age <- sl_estimated_abundance %>%
  select(survey_year, beach, short_label, est_abundance, log_est,
         spawn_lag_min, spawn_lag_max, n_clams, pct) %>%
  mutate(
    beach = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE)
  )

cat("Age-class response table:", nrow(rec_age), "rows\n")
cat("Age classes:", paste(unique(rec_age$short_label), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Response variable: log1p(est_abundance) — beach-wide population estimate\n")

# ── Run age-class-specific lag correlations using monthly indices ─────────
# For each age class, we test ALL lags (0–max_lag) but mark which lags
# fall within the biologically expected window for that age class.
# This lets us see if the data confirm the expected lag structure.

age_cor_results <- list()

for (i in 1:nrow(age_class_config)) {
  ac       <- age_class_config$short_label[i]
  lag_lo   <- age_class_config$spawn_lag_min[i]
  lag_hi   <- age_class_config$spawn_lag_max[i]
  
  # Get abundance for this age class
  rec_ac <- rec_age %>%
    filter(short_label == ac) %>%
    select(beach, sy = survey_year, est_abundance, log_est)
  
  # Join to environmental indices at each lag
  ac_lag <- map_dfr(lag_range, function(lg) {
    rec_ac %>%
      left_join(
        ti_monthly %>% mutate(sy = year + lg) %>% select(-year),
        by = c("beach", "sy")
      ) %>%
      mutate(lag = lg)
  })
  
  # Compute correlations for all predictors
  ac_cor <- ac_lag %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(tv_all), names_to = "temp_var", values_to = "temp_val") %>%
    group_by(beach, lag, temp_var) %>%
    summarise(
      n       = sum(!is.na(temp_val) & !is.na(log_est)),
      r       = cor_p(log_est, temp_val)["r"],
      p       = cor_p(log_est, temp_val)["p"],
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      window       = tv_labels[temp_var],
      metric       = metric_labels[temp_var],
      sig          = case_when(p < 0.001 ~ "***", p < 0.01 ~ "**",
                                p < 0.05  ~ "*",   TRUE      ~ ""),
      age_class    = ac,
      in_bio_window = lag >= lag_lo & lag <= lag_hi
    )
  
  age_cor_results[[ac]] <- ac_cor
}

age_cor_all <- bind_rows(age_cor_results) %>%
  mutate(age_class = factor(age_class, levels = age_class_config$short_label))

cat("\n--- Age-class lag correlations computed ---\n")
cat("Total correlation rows:", nrow(age_cor_all), "\n")
cat("Age classes:", paste(levels(age_cor_all$age_class), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## 23b. Save age-class correlation matrices to Excel

```{r}
# ── One workbook per age class, sheets per beach ─────────────────────────
for (ac in age_class_config$short_label) {
  
  ac_sub <- age_cor_all %>%
    filter(age_class == ac) %>%
    select(beach, lag, window, metric, r, p, sig, n, in_bio_window) %>%
    mutate(across(c(r), ~round(., 3)),
           across(c(p), ~round(., 4))) %>%
    arrange(beach, metric, window, lag)
  
  wb_ac <- createWorkbook()
  addWorksheet(wb_ac, "All_Beaches")
  writeData(wb_ac, "All_Beaches", ac_sub)
  
  for (bch in beach_order) {
    bch_data <- ac_sub %>% filter(beach == bch)
    if (nrow(bch_data) > 0) {
      addWorksheet(wb_ac, gsub(" ", "_", bch))
      writeData(wb_ac, gsub(" ", "_", bch), bch_data)
    }
  }
  
  saveWorkbook(wb_ac, file.path(folder_name, "excel",
                                 paste0("lag_correlations_", tolower(ac), ".xlsx")),
               overwrite = TRUE)
}

cat("Saved age-class correlation workbooks to excel/\n")
```

## 24a. Best-lag heatmap per age class (analogous to Section 10 for recruits)

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=10}
for (ac in age_class_config$short_label) {
  
  ac_cfg <- age_class_config %>% filter(short_label == ac)
  
  # Find best lag per beach × metric × window
  best_lag_ac <- age_cor_all %>%
    filter(age_class == ac) %>%
    group_by(beach, metric, window) %>%
    slice_max(abs(r), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      label = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", r), sig, "\nL", lag),
      beach = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE),
      metric = factor(metric, levels = metric_levels)
    )
  
  p_best_ac <- best_lag_ac %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = beach, y = window, fill = r)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_tile(data = . %>% filter(p < 0.05),
              fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.8, color = "black") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                         midpoint = 0, limits = c(-0.8, 0.8), name = "Pearson r") +
    facet_wrap(~metric, nrow = 1) +
    labs(x     = "Beach (North → South)",
         y     = "Seasonal window",
         title = paste0(ac, " — Best-lag correlation heatmap"),
         subtitle = paste0("Expected spawning lags: ", ac_cfg$spawn_lag_min,
                           "–", ac_cfg$spawn_lag_max, " years | ",
                           "Black outlines = p < 0.05 | L# = lag year")) +
    my_theme +
    theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
          strip.text       = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
          axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 10, angle = 35, hjust = 1))
  
  print(p_best_ac)
  if (save_age_heatmaps) {
    ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "age_class_heatmaps",
                     paste0("best_lag_heatmap_", tolower(ac), ".png")),
           plot = p_best_ac, width = 16, height = 8, dpi = 300)
  }
}
```

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=10}
for (ac in age_class_config$short_label) {
```

## 25a. Predictor selection for each age class

```{r}
# ── Select top 2 predictors per age class × beach ────────────────────────
# Uses bio-window-restricted correlations to select the strongest predictors
# at biologically appropriate lags.

age_pred_selections <- bio_best %>%
  group_by(age_class, beach) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(r))) %>%
  slice_head(n = 2) %>%
  mutate(pred_rank = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(age_class, beach, pred_rank, temp_var, metric, window, lag, r, p, sig)

cat("\n--- Top 2 predictors per age class × beach ---\n")
age_pred_selections %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(metric, " ", window, " L", lag, " r=", round(r, 2), sig)) %>%
  select(age_class, beach, pred_rank, label) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = pred_rank, values_from = label,
              names_prefix = "Pred_") %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

## 25b. Fit age-class-specific models

```{r}
# ── Build and evaluate models for each age class × beach ──────────────────

# Helper: build model data for one age class × beach combo
build_age_model_data <- function(beach_name, ac_label, preds, rec_lag_data, rec_age_df) {
  
  pred_sub <- preds %>%
    filter(age_class == ac_label, beach == beach_name)
  
  if (nrow(pred_sub) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  # Response: log-transformed abundance for this age class at this beach
  resp <- rec_age_df %>%
    filter(short_label == ac_label, beach == beach_name) %>%
    select(sy = survey_year, est_abundance, log_est) %>%
    rename(log_resp = log_est) %>%
    arrange(sy)
  
  if (nrow(resp) < 8) return(NULL)
  
  # Density-dependence: lagged response
  resp <- resp %>%
    mutate(log_resp_lag1 = lag(log_resp, 1))
  
  # Join predictors
  md <- resp
  for (i in 1:min(nrow(pred_sub), 2)) {
    tvar <- pred_sub$temp_var[i]
    lg   <- pred_sub$lag[i]
    pid  <- paste0("env", i)
    
    pred_data <- ti_monthly %>%
      filter(beach == beach_name) %>%
      mutate(sy = year + lg) %>%
      select(sy, all_of(tvar)) %>%
      rename(!!pid := !!tvar)
    
    md <- md %>% left_join(pred_data, by = "sy")
  }
  
  attr(md, "beach")     <- beach_name
  attr(md, "age_class") <- ac_label
  attr(md, "pred1_label") <- paste0(pred_sub$metric[1], " ", pred_sub$window[1], " L", pred_sub$lag[1])
  attr(md, "pred2_label") <- ifelse(nrow(pred_sub) >= 2,
                                     paste0(pred_sub$metric[2], " ", pred_sub$window[2], " L", pred_sub$lag[2]), NA)
  return(md)
}

# ── Fit models for all age class × beach combinations ────────────────────
age_model_results <- list()

for (ac in age_class_config$short_label) {
  for (bch in beach_order) {
    
    key <- paste(bch, ac, sep = " | ")
    md <- build_age_model_data(bch, ac, age_pred_selections, NULL, rec_age)
    if (is.null(md)) next
    
    has_env2 <- "env2" %in% names(md) && any(!is.na(md$env2))
    
    formulas <- list(
      "Null"      = log_resp ~ 1,
      "Env1"      = log_resp ~ env1,
      "Env1 + DD" = log_resp ~ env1 + log_resp_lag1
    )
    
    if (has_env2) {
      formulas[["Env1 + Env2"]]      <- log_resp ~ env1 + env2
      formulas[["Env1 + Env2 + DD"]] <- log_resp ~ env1 + env2 + log_resp_lag1
      formulas[["Env2"]]             <- log_resp ~ env2
    }
    formulas[["DD only"]] <- log_resp ~ log_resp_lag1
    
    model_fits  <- list()
    model_stats <- list()
    
    for (mname in names(formulas)) {
      needed_vars <- all.vars(formulas[[mname]])
      md_complete <- md %>% select(sy, all_of(needed_vars)) %>% na.omit()
      if (nrow(md_complete) < 8) next
      
      fit <- tryCatch(lm(formulas[[mname]], data = md_complete), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(fit)) next
      
      r2     <- summary(fit)$r.squared
      adj_r2 <- summary(fit)$adj.r.squared
      aicc   <- tryCatch(AICc(fit), error = function(e) NA)
      
      cv_loo  <- tryCatch(loocv(formulas[[mname]], md_complete),
                           error = function(e) list(q2 = NA, rmse = NA))
      cv_roll <- tryCatch(rolling_cv(formulas[[mname]], md_complete),
                           error = function(e) list(q2 = NA, rmse = NA))
      
      model_fits[[mname]] <- fit
      model_stats[[mname]] <- tibble(
        model = mname, n = nobs(fit), k = length(coef(fit)),
        R2 = round(r2, 3), adj_R2 = round(adj_r2, 3),
        AICc = round(aicc, 1),
        Q2_LOOCV = round(cv_loo$q2, 3), RMSE_LOOCV = round(cv_loo$rmse, 3),
        Q2_rolling = round(cv_roll$q2, 3)
      )
    }
    
    if (length(model_stats) == 0) next
    
    stats_df <- bind_rows(model_stats) %>%
      mutate(delta_AICc = round(AICc - min(AICc, na.rm = TRUE), 1)) %>%
      arrange(AICc)
    
    age_model_results[[key]] <- list(
      beach = bch, age_class = ac,
      model_data = md,
      pred1_label = attr(md, "pred1_label"),
      pred2_label = attr(md, "pred2_label"),
      formulas = formulas, fits = model_fits,
      stats = stats_df, best_model = stats_df$model[1]
    )
    
    cat("\n--- ", key, " ---\n")
    cat("Best model:", stats_df$model[1], "| R²:", stats_df$R2[1],
        "| Q²(LOOCV):", stats_df$Q2_LOOCV[1], "\n")
  }
}
```

## 25d. Diagnostic plots for age-class models

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=20}
for (key in names(age_model_results)) {
  
  res   <- age_model_results[[key]]
  bfit  <- res$fits[[res$best_model]]
  md    <- res$model_data
  bch   <- res$beach
  ac    <- res$age_class
  
  if (is.null(bfit)) next
  
  needed <- all.vars(res$formulas[[res$best_model]])
  md_complete <- md %>% select(sy, all_of(needed)) %>% na.omit()
  if (nrow(md_complete) < 5) next
  
  md_complete$fitted   <- fitted(bfit)
  md_complete$residual <- residuals(bfit)
  
  cv_loo <- tryCatch(loocv(res$formulas[[res$best_model]], md_complete),
                      error = function(e) list(predicted = rep(NA, nrow(md_complete)), q2 = NA))
  md_complete$loo_pred <- cv_loo$predicted
  
  # Panel 1: Observed vs Predicted
  p1 <- md_complete %>%
    select(sy, Observed = log_resp, Fitted = fitted, LOOCV = loo_pred) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(Fitted, LOOCV), names_to = "type", values_to = "predicted") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = predicted, y = Observed, color = type)) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, lty = 2, color = "grey50") +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Fitted = "firebrick", LOOCV = "steelblue")) +
    labs(x = "Predicted", y = "Observed", title = "Observed vs Predicted", color = NULL) +
    my_theme + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  # Panel 2: Time series fit
  p2 <- md_complete %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = sy)) +
    geom_line(aes(y = log_resp), color = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(aes(y = log_resp), color = "black", size = 2) +
    geom_line(aes(y = fitted), color = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.7, lty = 2) +
    geom_line(aes(y = loo_pred), color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.7, lty = 3) +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "log(abundance + 1)",
         title = "Predicted time series (black=obs, red=fitted, blue=LOOCV)") +
    my_theme
  
  # Panel 3: Residuals
  p3 <- md_complete %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = fitted, y = residual)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lty = 2) +
    geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.6) +
    labs(x = "Fitted", y = "Residuals", title = "Residuals vs Fitted") +
    my_theme
  
  # Panel 4: Q-Q
  p4 <- md_complete %>%
    mutate(theoretical = qqnorm(residual, plot.it = FALSE)$x,
           sample      = qqnorm(residual, plot.it = FALSE)$y) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = theoretical, y = sample)) +
    geom_abline(intercept = mean(md_complete$residual),
                slope = sd(md_complete$residual), lty = 2, color = "grey50") +
    geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(x = "Theoretical", y = "Sample", title = "Normal Q-Q") +
    my_theme
  
  p_diag <- (p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = paste0(bch, " — ", ac),
      subtitle = paste0("Best: ", res$best_model, " | R²=", round(summary(bfit)$r.squared, 3),
                        " | Q²=", round(cv_loo$q2, 3),
                        " | Pred1: ", res$pred1_label),
      theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"))
    )
  
  print(p_diag)
  if (save_age_models) {
    fname <- paste0("diag_", gsub(" ", "_", tolower(bch)), "_",
                    tolower(ac), ".png")
    ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "age_class_models", fname),
           plot = p_diag, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 300)
  }
}
```

## 26a. Cohort tracking: follow YOY pulse through subsequent years

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=14}
# ── Track large YOY cohorts as they age through size classes ──────────────
# A strong YOY year should produce a strong Juvenile year +1, then Sub-adult
# year +2–3, etc. This validates the age-class assignments.

# Compute relative YOY abundance (z-score within beach) to identify big years
yoy_z <- sl_estimated_abundance %>%
  filter(short_label == "YOY") %>%
  group_by(beach) %>%
  mutate(z_yoy = scale(est_abundance)[,1]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(survey_year, beach, z_yoy, est_yoy = est_abundance)

# For each big YOY year (z > 1), track what happens to Juvenile, Sub-adult, Adult
big_yoy_years <- yoy_z %>%
  filter(z_yoy > 1) %>%
  select(spawn_year = survey_year, beach)

# Build cohort tracking table
cohort_track <- list()
for (i in 1:nrow(big_yoy_years)) {
  sy  <- big_yoy_years$spawn_year[i]
  bch <- big_yoy_years$beach[i]
  
  track <- sl_estimated_abundance %>%
    filter(beach == bch,
           (short_label == "YOY"       & survey_year == sy) |
           (short_label == "Juvenile"   & survey_year %in% (sy + 1):(sy + 2)) |
           (short_label == "Sub-adult"  & survey_year %in% (sy + 2):(sy + 3)) |
           (short_label == "Adult"      & survey_year %in% (sy + 3):(sy + 5))) %>%
    mutate(cohort_year = sy, years_since_yoy = survey_year - sy)
  
  cohort_track[[i]] <- track
}

cohort_df <- bind_rows(cohort_track) %>%
  mutate(
    short_label = factor(short_label, levels = age_class_config$short_label),
    beach = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE),
    cohort_label = paste0(beach, " ", cohort_year)
  )

if (nrow(cohort_df) > 0) {
  # Normalize within each cohort for comparison
  cohort_df <- cohort_df %>%
    group_by(cohort_label) %>%
    mutate(rel_abundance = est_abundance / max(est_abundance, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  p_cohort <- cohort_df %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = years_since_yoy, y = rel_abundance,
               color = beach, group = cohort_label)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
    stat_summary(aes(group = beach), fun = mean,
                 geom = "line", linewidth = 1.5) +
    stat_summary(aes(group = beach), fun = mean,
                 geom = "point", size = 3) +
    scale_color_manual(values = beach_colors, name = "Beach") +
    facet_wrap(~beach, ncol = 1) +
    labs(x     = "Years since YOY peak",
         y     = "Relative abundance (proportion of peak)",
         title = "Cohort tracking: how large YOY pulses decay through age classes",
         subtitle = paste0("Faint lines = individual cohorts (YOY z-score > 1) | ",
                           "Bold = beach mean\n",
                           "Steeper decline = higher mortality between stages")) +
    my_theme +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
          strip.text       = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))
  
  print(p_cohort)
  if (save_cohort) {
    ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "cohort_tracking", "cohort_decay_curves.png"),
           plot = p_cohort, width = 14, height = 14, dpi = 300)
  }
}
```

## 26b. Lagged cross-correlation: YOY predicting future age classes

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# ── Does this year's YOY predict next year's Juvenile, etc.? ──────────────
# Positive r at the right lag confirms age progression.

yoy_juv_lag <- list()

for (bch in beach_order) {
  
  yoy_ts <- sl_estimated_abundance %>%
    filter(beach == bch, short_label == "YOY") %>%
    select(survey_year, est_yoy = est_abundance) %>%
    arrange(survey_year)
  
  for (ac in c("Juvenile", "Sub-adult", "Adult")) {
    ac_ts <- sl_estimated_abundance %>%
      filter(beach == bch, short_label == ac) %>%
      select(survey_year, est_ac = est_abundance) %>%
      arrange(survey_year)
    
    for (lg in 0:5) {
      joined <- yoy_ts %>%
        mutate(target_year = survey_year + lg) %>%
        inner_join(ac_ts, by = c("target_year" = "survey_year"))
      
      if (nrow(joined) > 5) {
        ct <- cor_p(log1p(joined$est_yoy), log1p(joined$est_ac))
        yoy_juv_lag <- c(yoy_juv_lag, list(tibble(
          beach = bch, target_class = ac, lag = lg,
          r = ct["r"], p = ct["p"], n = nrow(joined)
        )))
      }
    }
  }
}

yoy_progression <- bind_rows(yoy_juv_lag) %>%
  mutate(
    beach = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE),
    target_class = factor(target_class, levels = c("Juvenile", "Sub-adult", "Adult")),
    sig = case_when(p < 0.001 ~ "***", p < 0.01 ~ "**", p < 0.05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")
  )

p_yoy_prog <- yoy_progression %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lag, y = r, color = beach)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = ifelse(p < 0.05, "sig", "ns")), size = 3) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(sig = 16, ns = 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = beach_colors, name = "Beach (N → S)") +
  facet_wrap(~target_class, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x     = "Lag (years after YOY survey)",
       y     = "Pearson r (log YOY vs log target class)",
       title = "YOY → future age class progression: does a strong settlement persist?",
       subtitle = paste0("Juvenile should peak at lag 1 | Sub-adult at lag 1–2 | Adult at lag 2–5\n",
                         "Filled points = p < 0.05")) +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position  = "right",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))

print(p_yoy_prog)
if (save_cohort) {
  ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "cohort_tracking", "yoy_progression_lags.png"),
         plot = p_yoy_prog, width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 300)
}

# Save to Excel
wb_prog <- createWorkbook()
addWorksheet(wb_prog, "YOY_Progression")
writeData(wb_prog, "YOY_Progression", yoy_progression %>%
            mutate(r = round(r, 3), p = round(p, 4)))
saveWorkbook(wb_prog, file.path(folder_name, "excel",
                                 "yoy_cohort_progression.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
```

## 26d. Environmental smoking gun — best predictor overlay per age class

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=20}
# ── For each age class, overlay the best environmental predictor (z-scored) ──
# against the age-class abundance time series at each beach.

for (ac in age_class_config$short_label) {
  
  overlay_plots <- list()
  
  for (bch in beach_order) {
    
    key <- paste(bch, ac, sep = " | ")
    if (!key %in% names(age_model_results)) next
    
    res <- age_model_results[[key]]
    pred_sel <- age_pred_selections %>%
      filter(age_class == ac, beach == bch, pred_rank == 1)
    
    if (nrow(pred_sel) == 0) next
    
    tvar <- pred_sel$temp_var
    lg   <- pred_sel$lag
    
    # Age class abundance
    abund <- rec_age %>%
      filter(short_label == ac, beach == bch) %>%
      select(sy = survey_year, est_abundance) %>%
      mutate(z_abund = scale(est_abundance)[,1])
    
    # Environmental predictor at optimal lag
    env_ts <- ti_monthly %>%
      filter(beach == bch) %>%
      select(year, all_of(tvar)) %>%
      rename(env_val = !!tvar) %>%
      mutate(sy = year + lg,
             z_env = scale(env_val)[,1])
    
    joined <- abund %>%
      left_join(env_ts %>% select(sy, z_env), by = "sy") %>%
      mutate(beach = bch)
    
    overlay_plots[[bch]] <- joined
  }
  
  if (length(overlay_plots) == 0) next
  
  overlay_dat_ac <- bind_rows(overlay_plots) %>%
    mutate(beach = factor(beach, levels = beach_order, ordered = TRUE))
  
  # Get labels for each beach
  pred_labels <- age_pred_selections %>%
    filter(age_class == ac, pred_rank == 1) %>%
    mutate(label = paste0(metric, " ", window, " L", lag, " (r=", round(r, 2), sig, ")")) %>%
    select(beach, label)
  
  overlay_dat_ac <- overlay_dat_ac %>%
    left_join(pred_labels, by = "beach")
  
  p_overlay_ac <- overlay_dat_ac %>%
    select(beach, sy, z_abund, z_env, label) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(z_abund, z_env),
                 names_to = "series", values_to = "z") %>%
    mutate(series = recode(series,
                            z_abund = paste0(ac, " abundance"),
                            z_env   = "Environmental predictor")) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = sy, y = z, color = series, linewidth = series)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey60") +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("firebrick", "steelblue"),
                       name = NULL) +
    scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(1.2, 0.7), guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~beach + label, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x     = "Survey year",
         y     = "Z-score (standard deviations from mean)",
         title = paste0(ac, " — environmental predictor overlay (z-scored)"),
         subtitle = "When lines track each other, environment drives abundance at the expected lag") +
    my_theme +
    theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = "black"),
          strip.text       = element_text(size = 10))
  
  print(p_overlay_ac)
  if (save_cohort) {
    ggsave(file.path(folder_name, "population_structure",
                     paste0("env_overlay_", tolower(ac), ".png")),
           plot = p_overlay_ac, width = 14, height = 16, dpi = 300)
  }
}
```
